b: Speaker Aamir Amin is a Bachelor of Arts in History from Kashmir University.
f: Speaker Aamir Amin is a Bachelor of Arts in History from Kashmir University.

b: Speaker Abodh Aras is the Chief Executive Officer of The Welfare of Stray Dogs (WSD), a pioneering Mumbai-based animal welfare NGO. With over 25 years of leadership, he has played a key role in transforming city’s…
f: Speaker Abodh Aras is the Chief Executive Officer of The Welfare of Stray Dogs (WSD), a pioneering Mumbai-based animal welfare NGO. With over 25 years of leadership, he has played a key role in transforming city’s approach towards the care and management of its street dog population. A former corporate professional, he brings a unique perspective on how compassion, civic engagement, and professional management can come together to create lasting social change. His book, My City, My Dogs (2021), introduces children to the street dogs of Mumbai. He was a recipient of The Rotary Club of Bombay’s Social Service Award (2024) and the Free Press Journal’s Angels of Mumbai Award (2025).

b: Speaker Aditi Krishnakumar has published seven books, including the YA historical novel The White Lotus (2025). She is also the co-author of four scholarly articles on mathematics. She is a recipient of the Scholastic…
f: Speaker Aditi Krishnakumar has published seven books, including the YA historical novel The White Lotus (2025). She is also the co-author of four scholarly articles on mathematics. She is a recipient of the Scholastic Asian Book Award and the Young Alumni Achievers Award from IIM Ahmedabad. She has been nominated for the Singapore Book Prize, the Asian Scientist Writing Prize, and the Binod Kanoria Award for Children’s Literature. She holds an MSc in Mathematics, an MA in English, an MBA, and an LLB and is working towards a PhD in Mathematics. She worked in finance for several years in India and Singapore.

b: Speaker Aditya Deshbandhu is a Senior Lecturer of Communications, Digital Media Sociology at the University of Exeter, UK. A researcher of video game studies, new media, and the digital divide, he examines how people…
f: Speaker Aditya Deshbandhu is a Senior Lecturer of Communications, Digital Media Sociology at the University of Exeter, UK. A researcher of video game studies, new media, and the digital divide, he examines how people engage with digital artifacts to understand how these interactions shape everyday lives. He is the author of Gaming Culture(s) in India: Digital Play in Everyday Life (2020) and The 21st Century in 100 Games ( 2024) . He also serves as an editor on the book series – Games and Contemporary Culture, and the now 8-year-long running weekly column ‘Game On’ for Telangana Today .

b: Speaker Afsar Mohammad writes poetry and short fiction in Telugu and English. Evening With a Sufi (2022) is a translation of his poetry, and Sahil Will Come and Other Stories (2025), a collection of his short stories in…
f: Speaker Afsar Mohammad writes poetry and short fiction in Telugu and English. Evening With a Sufi (2022) is a translation of his poetry, and Sahil Will Come and Other Stories (2025), a collection of his short stories in translation. His other publications include The Festival of Pirs: Popular Islam and Shared Devotion in South India (2013) and Remaking History: 1948 Police Action and the Muslims of Hyderabad (2023).

b: Speaker Alankrita Amaya is an award-winning children’s book writer and illustrator. Her publications include Little Laali (2013), Chuglubugloo (2019), Muft Ki Kulfi (2020), and Boodabim (2023). She grew up with a steady…
f: Speaker Alankrita Amaya is an award-winning children’s book writer and illustrator. Her publications include Little Laali (2013), Chuglubugloo (2019), Muft Ki Kulfi (2020), and Boodabim (2023). She grew up with a steady diet of picture books and found her life’s calling in storytelling through illustrations. Apart from weaving stories and illustrating wonder, she is also the co-founder of Hallubol, an initiative that preserves local Dakhni culture through bilingual comics and picture books rooted in the everyday experiences of South Indian Dakhni-speaking communities.

b: Speaker Alina Gufran is an author and filmmaker. Her debut novel, No Place To Call My Own (2025), was on the longlist of the Godrej Lit Live Award for Best Debut. Her film, Leela (2024), premiered at IFFR and played at…
f: Speaker Alina Gufran is an author and filmmaker. Her debut novel, No Place To Call My Own (2025), was on the longlist of the Godrej Lit Live Award for Best Debut. Her film, Leela (2024), premiered at IFFR and played at San Sebastian International Film Festival, Dokufest, Riga International Film Festival, and MAMI, among others.

b: Speaker Alokparna Sengupta is the Managing Director of Humane World for Animals India Foundation (formerly known as Humane Society International). She served on government and scientific committees, leading efforts to…
f: Speaker Alokparna Sengupta is the Managing Director of Humane World for Animals India Foundation (formerly known as Humane Society International). She served on government and scientific committees, leading efforts to ban cosmetic testing on animals and improve farm animal welfare. A skilled trainer in animal law, she has trained magistrates, police, and advocates, and trained children from ages 4-6 to 12-15 on animal welfare. She worked with Thomson Reuters and FIAPO, and is a certified POSH trainer. She was featured in ‘Hundred and One Reasons to Get Out of Bed’ and has published a children’s story on compassion towards animals for Pratham Books.

b: Speaker Ameer Shahul focuses on healthcare and climate change. His debut book, Heavy Metal: How a Global Corporation Poisoned Kodaikanal (2023), won the GreenLitFest Book of the Year Award 2024 and was longlisted for…
f: Speaker Ameer Shahul focuses on healthcare and climate change. His debut book, Heavy Metal: How a Global Corporation Poisoned Kodaikanal (2023), won the GreenLitFest Book of the Year Award 2024 and was longlisted for the Tata Literature Live! Awards 2023. It was translated into Tamil and is being adapted into a feature film in Hindi by Netflix. His second book, Vaccine Nation: How Immunisation Shaped India (2025), traces India’s two centuries of vaccine journey. His next book, The Silent Syndicate (2026), which explores the Western capture of Indian healthcare, is followed by Liquid Empire (2027). He held leadership roles in global corporations and was a journalist with international newswires.

b: Speaker Amita Talwar is the founding editor and publisher of Channel 6 , Hyderabad’s first monthly magazine. A course in filmmaking at New York University led to a documentary on Kaifi Azmi. Her photographs were…
f: Speaker Amita Talwar is the founding editor and publisher of Channel 6 , Hyderabad’s first monthly magazine. A course in filmmaking at New York University led to a documentary on Kaifi Azmi. Her photographs were exhibited in India and at the Wendt Gallery in New York, and published as a book, Forms of the Formless (2010). ‘Veils and Palimpsests: Kashmir 2025’, an exhibition of her work, is currently on at the Gandhi Memorial Centre in Bethesda, Washington DC. She founded Art For Causes (2014), which launched Shabd Shala in collaboration with the Kabir Project (2023). Her current initiative is ‘Main Pal Do Pal Ka Shayar Hoon’, a play on Sahir Ludhianvi.

b: Speaker Anand Kumar K , a PhD in Microbiology, has over 33 years of experience in the vaccine/biotech Industry. He worked abroad for Pfizer Global Manufacturing, Australia, and Schering Plough (now MSD) Animal Health ,…
f: Speaker Anand Kumar K , a PhD in Microbiology, has over 33 years of experience in the vaccine/biotech Industry. He worked abroad for Pfizer Global Manufacturing, Australia, and Schering Plough (now MSD) Animal Health , New Zealand. Currently, he is the Managing Director at Indian Immunologicals Ltd, one of the largest producers of vaccines in Asia. Several important human and animal vaccines were developed under his leadership and he also established Pristine Biologicals in New Zealand to help India secure a key raw material used in vaccine manufacturing. He is a member of several committees in India and has many awards, papers, and patents to his credit.

b: Speaker Anand Neelakantan is the author of the popular Bahubali trilogy, the prequel to S. S. Rajamouli’s movie. He is also the author of Asura: Tale of the Vanquished (2012), a retelling of the Ramayana from Ravana’s…
f: Speaker Anand Neelakantan is the author of the popular Bahubali trilogy, the prequel to S. S. Rajamouli’s movie. He is also the author of Asura: Tale of the Vanquished (2012), a retelling of the Ramayana from Ravana’s point of view, and the Ajaya series, which told the Mahabharata from Duryodhana’s perspective. Vanara (2018), Valmiki’s Women (2021), Nala Damayanti (2023), The Tale of the Flying Mountains (2023), and the latest Many Ramayanas, Many Lessons (2025) are his other popular works. His books have been translated into more than fifteen languages, including Indonesian and Burmese. He has also written scripts and screenplays for TV and columns for newspapers.

b: Speaker Anindita Bhadra is a behavioural biologist who studies the street dogs of India. She is a Professor at the Department of Biological Sciences at IISER Kolkata. She was the founding chairperson of the Indian…
f: Speaker Anindita Bhadra is a behavioural biologist who studies the street dogs of India. She is a Professor at the Department of Biological Sciences at IISER Kolkata. She was the founding chairperson of the Indian National Young Academy of Science and served as a co-chair of the Global Young Academy. She is actively engaged in science outreach and is a thespian.

b: Speaker Anjal Prakash is a Clinical Associate Professor (Research) and Research Director at the Bharti Institute of Public Policy (BIPP), Indian School of Business (ISB). An experienced researcher and academic, his work…
f: Speaker Anjal Prakash is a Clinical Associate Professor (Research) and Research Director at the Bharti Institute of Public Policy (BIPP), Indian School of Business (ISB). An experienced researcher and academic, his work primarily focuses on water and climate change, urban resilience, gender, and social inclusion in South Asia. He is an IPCC author and contributes to their report.

b: Speaker Anjali Monteiro is a documentary filmmaker, researcher, and teacher. She is the joint winner (with KP Jayasankar) of 33 national and international awards, the most recent being the Jury’s commendation in the…
f: Speaker Anjali Monteiro is a documentary filmmaker, researcher, and teacher. She is the joint winner (with KP Jayasankar) of 33 national and international awards, the most recent being the Jury’s commendation in the Intangible Culture category for A Delicate Weave at the Royal Anthropological Institute Festival, UK, 2019. She co-authored the national award-winning book A Fly in the Curry: Independent Documentary Film in India (2016). She retired as Professor and Dean from the School of Media and Cultural Studies, Tata Institute of Social Sciences, Mumbai. She received a Lifetime Achievement Award for Outstanding Contribution to Film Education from the National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad, India.

b: Speaker Anju Khemani founded the Drama Association of the Deaf (DAD) in 2013. It is a collective that aims to build a new form of theatrical expression by introducing Deaf culture to the creative world of drama. She has…
f: Speaker Anju Khemani founded the Drama Association of the Deaf (DAD) in 2013. It is a collective that aims to build a new form of theatrical expression by introducing Deaf culture to the creative world of drama. She has worked towards educating, supporting, and leading people and organizations to build a creative and communicative world of change in different areas– education, women empowerment, disability, and theatre–in corporate, media, and NGO Sector. DAD was an outcome of her theatre course at the National School of Drama and extensive work with the Deaf community.

b: Speaker Ankit Wali graduated in Mass Media in 2021 from RD National College, Mumbai. He began his journey in the performing arts through theatre and playwriting before stepping into the industry as a Kashmiri Dialect…
f: Speaker Ankit Wali graduated in Mass Media in 2021 from RD National College, Mumbai. He began his journey in the performing arts through theatre and playwriting before stepping into the industry as a Kashmiri Dialect Coach, working with actors like Aparshakti Khurana and Satyajeet Dubey. He transitioned into assistant directing for web series and commercials, with his latest work being ‘The Broken News – Season 2’. He has also served as a Story Producer for popular television shows, including Big Boss. Along with Siddarth Koul, he combines their experience in fiction, documentary, theatre, and mainstream entertainment to tell rooted, emotional stories that resonate across borders.

b: Speaker Anup Surendranath is a professor of law at NALSAR University of Law Hyderabad where he teaches courses on Constitutional Law, Criminal Law, and the Law of Evidence. He is also the co-founder and Executive…
f: Speaker Anup Surendranath is a professor of law at NALSAR University of Law Hyderabad where he teaches courses on Constitutional Law, Criminal Law, and the Law of Evidence. He is also the co-founder and Executive Director of The Square Circle Clinic, a criminal justice initiative that provides pro bono legal representation to death row prisoners all across India and also to undertrials in Maharashtra. The Clinic’s work has resulted in 33 death row prisoners being acquitted by the Supreme Court and High Courts, and a further 54 individuals getting off death row through lowering of punishment. Their work has been recognised and awarded by the New York Legal Aid Society, the World Psychiatry Association, World Congress Against the Death Penalty, and most recently by the Delhi High Court Bar Association in December 2025.

b: Speaker Anuradha S. Naik is a UNESCO award-winning conservation architect, award-winning author, and Principal at Anuradha Naik Associates, Hyderabad. She studied at the Edinburgh College of Art and the Bartlett,…
f: Speaker Anuradha S. Naik is a UNESCO award-winning conservation architect, award-winning author, and Principal at Anuradha Naik Associates, Hyderabad. She studied at the Edinburgh College of Art and the Bartlett, University College London. She is a chartered member of the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA), the Royal Incorporation of Architects of Scotland (RIAS), a Fellow of the Royal Society of Arts (FRSA), and the Royal Asiatic Society (FRAS). Her work combines conservation, retrofitting, design, and curation of galleries. She has worked on major projects in the UK and in India, including the Laxmi Niwas Palace, Bikaner, the Chowmahalla Palace, the Taj Falaknuma Palace, the Domakonda Fort, and Purani Haveli.

b: Speaker Anusha Ramanathan is the author of The Little Book of Indian Dogs (2025) and Sarayu’s Museum Adventure (2025). She is a fourth-generation lawyer and a collector of picture books and antique jewellery. She…
f: Speaker Anusha Ramanathan is the author of The Little Book of Indian Dogs (2025) and Sarayu’s Museum Adventure (2025). She is a fourth-generation lawyer and a collector of picture books and antique jewellery. She inherited a love of dogs from her cynophile father, who was an encyclopaedia of various dog breeds, both Indian and foreign.

b: Speaker Anushka is pursuing an MA from The EFL University, Hyderabad.
f: Speaker Anushka is pursuing an MA from The EFL University, Hyderabad.

b: Speaker Aparna Gunti is a craftsperson and educator who, with her MCA and MA (Economics) degrees, brings an analytical and creative lens to her work. Her exploration of Kalamkari, the intricate and storied textile art…
f: Speaker Aparna Gunti is a craftsperson and educator who, with her MCA and MA (Economics) degrees, brings an analytical and creative lens to her work. Her exploration of Kalamkari, the intricate and storied textile art of India, led to a dedicated practice of learning, creating, and teaching. She conducts hands-on workshops that blend design thinking, sustainability, and cultural appreciation, helping participants transform Kalamkari fabric scraps into elegant, eco-friendly jewelry. Her sessions, for first-time crafters or with collaborating seasoned artisans, blend tradition and innovation, and foster an inclusive space where learners from diverse backgrounds discover the joy of wearable storytelling.

b: Speaker Aparna Rayaprol is at the Department of Sociology, University of Hyderabad, and served as the Head of the Department. A leading scholar in gender studies, urban sociology, and migration and diaspora, she has…
f: Speaker Aparna Rayaprol is at the Department of Sociology, University of Hyderabad, and served as the Head of the Department. A leading scholar in gender studies, urban sociology, and migration and diaspora, she has published Negotiating Identities: Women in the Indian Diaspora (1997), along with numerous other impactful publications. She holds a PhD from the University of Pittsburgh and pursued postdoctoral research at Princeton University’s Center for the Study of American Religion. Since the inception of the Study in India Program (SIP) in 1998, she has been at the heart of shaping global classrooms and intercultural learning at the University of Hyderabad.

b: Speaker Archana Chillala is a senior technologist based in Hyderabad with over nine years of industry experience, helping large enterprises evolve into modern digital businesses. Currently at NextIteration, she empowers…
f: Speaker Archana Chillala is a senior technologist based in Hyderabad with over nine years of industry experience, helping large enterprises evolve into modern digital businesses. Currently at NextIteration, she empowers teams to harness AI for delivering high-quality software with greater efficiency. She actively contributes to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion initiatives and has led internship programmes exclusively for the LGBTQI+ community and mentored women returning to the tech industry after career breaks. A dedicated runner since 2016, she regularly trains for and participates in long-distance running events, and has recently mentored a group of women to complete their first 5K run.

b: Speaker Arnab Barik is a neuroscientist at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, whose research focuses on the neural circuit mechanisms underlying pain, itch, stress, and affective behaviors. A central…
f: Speaker Arnab Barik is a neuroscientist at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, whose research focuses on the neural circuit mechanisms underlying pain, itch, stress, and affective behaviors. A central theme of his work is understanding how neuromodulatory systems, including serotonergic and dopaminergic pathways, shape sensory and motivational states in health and disease. His research has provided important insights into maladaptive plasticity in chronic pain and itch, with implications for developing targeted neuromodulatory therapies. He is the recipient of several competitive national and international fellowships and grants, reflecting the translational and conceptual significance of his work.

b: Speaker Arnav Maturi is a law student who is trying to balance the rigorous life of university with the finer things in life. When not attempting to memorise legal jargon or rehearse lines, he can usually be found with…
f: Speaker Arnav Maturi is a law student who is trying to balance the rigorous life of university with the finer things in life. When not attempting to memorise legal jargon or rehearse lines, he can usually be found with his nose buried in a book, pretending it is “research.” His hobbies include pretending that he is a good actor and excessive laziness.

b: Speaker Arshiya Sethi , independent scholar, cultural administrator, and artivist, leads in Indian performing arts. Formerly Creative Head at India Habitat Centre, she curated programs on classical/folk arts, civil…
f: Speaker Arshiya Sethi , independent scholar, cultural administrator, and artivist, leads in Indian performing arts. Formerly Creative Head at India Habitat Centre, she curated programs on classical/folk arts, civil society, and international festivals. A twice Fulbright Fellow, she served as dance critic for Times of India, Doordarshan advisor, and founder of Kri Foundation and Unmute (unmute.help) for arts-law advocacy and cultural equity. Co-author of Non-Gharanedaar: Pt. Mohanrao Kalyanpurkar, the Paviour of Kathak, she co-edited Dance Under the Shadow of the Nation with a Routledge book forthcoming. Founder-editor of South Asian Dance Intersections, she shared a deep bond with Kathak exponent Mangala Bhatt, co-curating Kri Foundation events blending artistry, scholarship, and discourse on dance as living heritage.

b: Speaker Arvind Menon is a long-time member of the Mirage Media team. He previously edited Occupied and Qubool Hai? He brings a restrained, investigative approach to his films, prioritising empathy and responsibility…
f: Speaker Arvind Menon is a long-time member of the Mirage Media team. He previously edited Occupied and Qubool Hai? He brings a restrained, investigative approach to his films, prioritising empathy and responsibility over spectacle.

b: Speaker Asad R. Rahmani was the Director of Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS), Executive Editor of Journal of BNHS , and Editor of BNHS magazines Hornbill , Mistnet , and Buceros . He is a Scientific Consultant to…
f: Speaker Asad R. Rahmani was the Director of Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS), Executive Editor of Journal of BNHS , and Editor of BNHS magazines Hornbill , Mistnet , and Buceros . He is a Scientific Consultant to The Corbett Foundation and Hem Chandra Mahindra Trust, served various MoEF committees, and was awarded Member of Honour by BirdLife International, UK. He has guided 11 PhDs, published 26 books, nearly 160 peer-reviewed scientific papers, 90 book reviews, nearly 75 editorials, and more than 350 popular articles on nature conservation. He was the Global Council member of BirdLife International, UK (2006-2013), and Chairman, BirdLife Asia Council (2006-2013). Living with Birds (2024) is his latest book.

b: Speaker Asaf Ali ’s passion for textiles began at fifteen, apprenticing under his uncle, a collector of fine carpets in Srinagar, Kashmir. He met art historian Jenny Housego, an avid collector and expert in tribal rugs,…
f: Speaker Asaf Ali ’s passion for textiles began at fifteen, apprenticing under his uncle, a collector of fine carpets in Srinagar, Kashmir. He met art historian Jenny Housego, an avid collector and expert in tribal rugs, who mentored him in the history of textiles. He joined her when she set out to trace how the fibre from Changra goats of Ladakh became the world’s finest pashmina. What began as exploration turned into a lifelong collaboration. Together, they founded Kashmir Loom, dedicated to revitalising traditional Kashmiri weaving while infusing it with innovation, whilst preserving the soul of pashmina as it evolves for the modern world.

b: Speaker Ashhar Farhan is a technologist and cultural entrepreneur, best known as one of the founders of Lamakaan , Hyderabad’s iconic open cultural space where artists, thinkers, and performers could freely present…
f: Speaker Ashhar Farhan is a technologist and cultural entrepreneur, best known as one of the founders of Lamakaan , Hyderabad’s iconic open cultural space where artists, thinkers, and performers could freely present their work. Established in 2010 with Humera Ahmed, Biju Mathew, and Elahe Hiptoola, Lamakaan has become a vibrant hub for dialogue, art, and inclusivity. His leadership has ensured it remains a sanctuary for progressive ideas, theater, music, and community engagement, making him a key figure in nurturing Hyderabad’s creative and intellectual landscape.

b: Speaker Atreya Sarma Uppaluri , Chief Editor ( Muse India literary ezine), is a poet, freelance editor, book reviewer, and translator. His poetry collection Sunny Rain-N-Snow (2016) was shortlisted for the Cochin…
f: Speaker Atreya Sarma Uppaluri , Chief Editor ( Muse India literary ezine), is a poet, freelance editor, book reviewer, and translator. His poetry collection Sunny Rain-N-Snow (2016) was shortlisted for the Cochin Litfest Poetry Prize 2019. He has edited 19 books in English and translated five major books from Telugu into English. From 2013 to 2018, he maintained a weekly poetry column, “Wordsmith”, in The Hans India English daily. He has received six literary awards, including one from the Department of Culture, Government of India, at the Rashtriya Sanskriti Mahotsav (2022), held in Hyderabad. Interested in holistic fitness, he has taken part in 23 organised runs so far.

b: Festival Director Dr B Kinnera Murthy is a strategy consultant, director on corporate boards and academic governing councils, national council member of professional organisations, and founder of a women support NGO,…
f: Festival Director Dr B Kinnera Murthy is a strategy consultant, director on corporate boards and academic governing councils, national council member of professional organisations, and founder of a women support NGO, among others. Since her superannuation in 2012 from the Administrative Staff College of India, where she held the posts of dean and professor of strategic management. She is also associated with Moving Images and Apna Watan. She is a director of the Hyderabad Literary Festival. Tejah Balantrapu Festival Director Usha Raman Festival Director Vijay Kumar Tadakamalla Festival Director

b: Speaker BS Prakash is a retired banker who is interested in reading both for himself and to others. He dabbles in amateur theatre, and is one of the founders of The Little Theatre Hyderabad, with whom he has been…
f: Speaker BS Prakash is a retired banker who is interested in reading both for himself and to others. He dabbles in amateur theatre, and is one of the founders of The Little Theatre Hyderabad, with whom he has been associated, he says, “for more years than he cares to remember, or can remember!”

b: Speaker Bakhtiar K Dadabhoy is the author of 10 books, including Jeh: A Life of JRD Tata (2005), Sugar in Milk: Lives of Eminent Parsis (2008), Barons of Banking (2013), Zubin Mehta: A Musical Journey (2016), The…
f: Speaker Bakhtiar K Dadabhoy is the author of 10 books, including Jeh: A Life of JRD Tata (2005), Sugar in Milk: Lives of Eminent Parsis (2008), Barons of Banking (2013), Zubin Mehta: A Musical Journey (2016), The Magnificent Diwan (2019), Homi J. Bhabha: A Life (2023), and Honest John: A Life of John Matthai (2025). He has also written the script for Nani: The Crusader (2015), a documentary on the legal luminary Nani A. Palkhivala. In 2024, he became the first non-scientist to deliver the annual Dr. K.S. Krishnan Memorial Lecture on the 125th birth anniversary of the physicist at NPL, New Delhi.

b: Speaker Bharath Guniganti is Head, Operations & Fact-checking Projects at Factly. He leads a team of fact-checkers dedicated to debunking viral misinformation across social media platforms. Additionally, he collaborates…
f: Speaker Bharath Guniganti is Head, Operations & Fact-checking Projects at Factly. He leads a team of fact-checkers dedicated to debunking viral misinformation across social media platforms. Additionally, he collaborates in formulating business strategy and policies and manages activities across departments, including finance, IT, and regulatory compliance. He is passionate about financial literacy and tries to educate people to protect themselves from falling prey to mis-selling in various financial products.

b: Speaker Bodhi is an artist, musician, and teacher whose work blends the boldness of ancient wisdom with a fiercely innovative approach to self-realization. His teachings, grounded in silence, self-inquiry, and deep…
f: Speaker Bodhi is an artist, musician, and teacher whose work blends the boldness of ancient wisdom with a fiercely innovative approach to self-realization. His teachings, grounded in silence, self-inquiry, and deep emotional processes, challenge the conditioned mind and expose the illusions of ego. Founder of Urvi, a forest community dedicated to conscious living, his approach is uncompromising and authentic. His recent book, Killing Buddha (2025), dismantles spiritual dogma and challenges the very pursuit of enlightenment, inviting seekers into a space of raw presence and honest self-reflection.

b: Speaker Chandra Shekhar Varma is a motivational speaker and author who writes in Hindi, English, and Urdu. He has inherited literature from his illustrious grandfather, Padma Bhushan Shri Bhagwati Charan Varma, and his…
f: Speaker Chandra Shekhar Varma is a motivational speaker and author who writes in Hindi, English, and Urdu. He has inherited literature from his illustrious grandfather, Padma Bhushan Shri Bhagwati Charan Varma, and his father, Shri Dhirendra Varma. His novel in English Corners of a Straight Line (2015) was a bestseller, his collection of stories in Hindi, Chaudah Left Chaudah Right (2022), was included in Sahitya Aaj Tak’s top ten books of 2023, and his collection of Urdu ghazals Ghat Rahi hai Roz meri Chehargi ’ has been published in 2025. He writes a regular column, ‘Gen Zen’ for The Times of India .

b: Speaker Chilakamarri Savitha is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Humanities at Mahindra University, Hyderabad. She has about 11 years of teaching experience, primarily instructing courses in English language,…
f: Speaker Chilakamarri Savitha is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Humanities at Mahindra University, Hyderabad. She has about 11 years of teaching experience, primarily instructing courses in English language, literature, and communication for both undergraduate and postgraduate students. She has edited and co-authored multiple books with reputable publishers, published in peer-reviewed journals, and presented research at major academic conferences.

b: Speaker Chinnaboina Pradeep Kumar is a wildlife filmmaker, photographer, and conservationist. He is the founder of Wild Telangana and Vwolfs Foundation, initiatives focused on conserving grasslands, wetlands, and…
f: Speaker Chinnaboina Pradeep Kumar is a wildlife filmmaker, photographer, and conservationist. He is the founder of Wild Telangana and Vwolfs Foundation, initiatives focused on conserving grasslands, wetlands, and lesser-known ecosystems beyond protected areas. His work uses visual storytelling to highlight habitat loss, human-wildlife coexistence, and conservation challenges in rural landscapes. He directed Indian Fox: Fighting Habitat Loss (2025) , Telangana’s first Telugu wildlife documentary, which draws attention to the rapid disappearance of grasslands and their native species. Through films, talks, and community engagement, he aims to inspire wider public participation in nature conservation.

b: Speaker Daneesh Majid concentrates on South Asian culture, security, and Urdu literature. He has worked for Siasat.com , the online English edition of the prominent Urdu daily. His writing has been featured in numerous…
f: Speaker Daneesh Majid concentrates on South Asian culture, security, and Urdu literature. He has worked for Siasat.com , the online English edition of the prominent Urdu daily. His writing has been featured in numerous South Asian media outlets, including Mint Lounge , The Hindu Business Line , Express Tribune , The New Indian Express , The Wire , The News Minute , The Print , Madras Courier , DailyO , The Nation (Pakistan), and Dhaka Tribune . He is an alumnus of Franklin and Marshall College, Pennsylvania, and the School of Oriental and African Studies (SOAS), University of London. The Hyderabadis: From 1947 to the Present Day (2025) is his first book.

b: Speaker Deepa Padmanaban is an independent journalist and author, writing on science, environment, biodiversity, wildlife conservation, public health, and climate change. Her stories have been published in The Guardian…
f: Speaker Deepa Padmanaban is an independent journalist and author, writing on science, environment, biodiversity, wildlife conservation, public health, and climate change. Her stories have been published in The Guardian , Harvard Public Health Magazine , Discover magazine, Scientific American , National Geographic , Mongabay , among others. She was a South Asia Speaks Fellow and Kiplinger Climate Fellow (USA) in 2022. She was awarded a special mention in the Environmental Impact category by the One World Media Awards (UK) in 2023. She worked as a biochemistry researcher at the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru, and Harvard University, USA. Invisible Housemates (2025) and Rewilding India (2025) are her recent publications.

b: Speaker Deepika Mahidhara describes herself as “a hatter who wears many hats and thrives on the energy she derives from juggling them all”. She is a learning & development consultant and a communications professional.…
f: Speaker Deepika Mahidhara describes herself as “a hatter who wears many hats and thrives on the energy she derives from juggling them all”. She is a learning & development consultant and a communications professional. She coaches individuals on life skills, personal leadership and public speaking, and facilitates workshops for adults on soft skills, behavioural skills and leadership skills. She is also a professional MC, talk-show host, content writer and an actor. She pursues her keen interest in theatre, music and most things art and culture. She loves the outdoors and is a novice motorcyclist.

b: Speaker Dhanya Rajendran is the co-founder and Editor-in-Chief of The News Minute , and the founding chairperson of DIGIPUB News India Foundation, which represents nearly 100 independent outlets, including The Wire ,…
f: Speaker Dhanya Rajendran is the co-founder and Editor-in-Chief of The News Minute , and the founding chairperson of DIGIPUB News India Foundation, which represents nearly 100 independent outlets, including The Wire , Scroll , Quint , and Newslaundry . She received the “Chameli Devi Jain Award for Outstanding Woman Journalist” (2022), the “Red Ink ‘Journalist of the Year’ Award” (2023), and was nominated for the “RSF (Reporters Without Borders) Impact Award” (2025) for her work defending press freedom and accountability journalism. The Global Investigative Journalism Network (GIJN) recognised her investigation into India’s electoral bonds as among the best investigative stories from India. The News Minute was also the first to uncover the voter roll manipulation scam.

b: Speaker Dinesh C. Sharma is an award-winning journalist and author with over 30 years of experience in reporting on science, technology, innovation, medicine, and environment-related issues for national and…
f: Speaker Dinesh C. Sharma is an award-winning journalist and author with over 30 years of experience in reporting on science, technology, innovation, medicine, and environment-related issues for national and international media outlets. He has written for various media houses and is a prolific author of various books. In June 2008, he had the privilege of becoming the first Asian journalist to go to the Arctic to report on an ongoing international scientific expedition relating to climate change. His current book is Space: The India Story (2025), profiling the fascinating story of India and Indians in space.

b: Speaker Emani Sivanagi Reddy is an archaeologist, sthapati, and CEO of Pleach India Foundation, renowned for transplanting over 100 heritage temples from Srisailam’s submerged area and building 100+ new ones per Shilpa…
f: Speaker Emani Sivanagi Reddy is an archaeologist, sthapati, and CEO of Pleach India Foundation, renowned for transplanting over 100 heritage temples from Srisailam’s submerged area and building 100+ new ones per Shilpa and Agama shastras. He served the Andhra Pradesh Archaeology & Museums Department for 35+ years, and was Director of National Institute of Tourism & Hospitality Management, State Gallery of Art, and OSD at Shilparamam. He also served on the Salar Jung Museum Board and Yadadri, Srisailam, Kanakadurga, and Kedarnath temple expert committees. He published 100+ books and 500+ articles and received Kalaratna (2018/2019), Vastusilpavachaspati, Bhasha Puraskaram (2018), and Kasinadhuni Desoddharaka Nageswararao Puraskaram (2019).

b: Speaker Endapalli Bharathi grew up in the fields with some spotty and irregular schooling, and today, apart from working on her farm and homestead, she writes fiction and works as a journalist for Navodayam , a magazine…
f: Speaker Endapalli Bharathi grew up in the fields with some spotty and irregular schooling, and today, apart from working on her farm and homestead, she writes fiction and works as a journalist for Navodayam , a magazine dedicated to women’s Self-Help Groups (SHGs). She writes in the Madanapalle Telugu dialect, depicting the struggles of Dalit women, their unique culture, social concerns, and the true landscape of rural life. Apart from short-story collections, she has also published a novel, Jakkiku (2023). She has won numerous awards for her work, including the Gidugu Rammurthy Puraskaram and the Bahujana Samajika Rachayitha Puraskaram.

b: Speaker Fazil NC is a Kerala-based filmmaker whose work explores the traditions and resilience of indigenous and traditional communities. He gained international recognition with In the Shade of Fallen Chinar and has…
f: Speaker Fazil NC is a Kerala-based filmmaker whose work explores the traditions and resilience of indigenous and traditional communities. He gained international recognition with In the Shade of Fallen Chinar and has served as a filmmaker-in-residence at the Basel Biennale, Switzerland, as well as a two-time jury member at the International Documentary and Short Film Festival of Kerala. His films have been screened at universities including Humboldt, Leipzig, Gothenburg, and New York University, and featured on National Geographic India and History TV. In addition to documentary filmmaking, Fazil has worked in the Malayalam film industry. His work highlights grassroots narratives and overlooked stories that exist beyond dominant and mainstream perspectives.

b: Speaker Vignesh is an interdisciplinary artist, writer, and curator whose practice engages with memory, ecology, and collective resistance. Trained in art history and painting, his work explores how embodied actions,…
f: Speaker Vignesh is an interdisciplinary artist, writer, and curator whose practice engages with memory, ecology, and collective resistance. Trained in art history and painting, his work explores how embodied actions, site-responsive interventions, and performative poetics can create spaces of care in the face of social and ecological crises. He is a founding member of Possible Futures, a collective that brings together visual artists, theatre practitioners, and students to create participatory, politically engaged art in public and contested spaces. His writings reflect his interest in performance studies, critical ecology, and South Asian contemporary art. He has contributed to exhibitions, festivals, and publications that foreground collective memory and cultural activism.

b: Speaker Gopalkrishna Gandhi studied English literature at St Stephen’s College, Delhi. A former administrator and diplomat, he has translated The Tirukkural (2015) from Tamil into English, Vikram Seth’s novel A Suitable…
f: Speaker Gopalkrishna Gandhi studied English literature at St Stephen’s College, Delhi. A former administrator and diplomat, he has translated The Tirukkural (2015) from Tamil into English, Vikram Seth’s novel A Suitable Boy into Hindi as कोई अच्छा सा लड़का ( Koi Achchha-Sa Ladka , 1998), authored a novel, Refuge (1989), and a play in English verse, Dara Shukoh (1993). He is currently a Distinguished Professor at Ashoka University.

b: Speaker Gopika Jadeja is a poet and translator working in English and Gujarati, and Coordinating Editor for PR&TA . A 2022 PEN Presents translation award winner, her new poetry collection is What Parvati Does Not Say…
f: Speaker Gopika Jadeja is a poet and translator working in English and Gujarati, and Coordinating Editor for PR&TA . A 2022 PEN Presents translation award winner, her new poetry collection is What Parvati Does Not Say (2025).

b: Speaker Greeshma Murthati is an illustrator from Hyderabad, India, currently working as a Research Associate at the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CSIR–CCMB). While her professional life revolves around…
f: Speaker Greeshma Murthati is an illustrator from Hyderabad, India, currently working as a Research Associate at the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CSIR–CCMB). While her professional life revolves around research that contributes to laying the platform for mRNA vaccine development, her artistic practice offers a parallel world shaped by intuition, colour, and creative exploration. She started Geetha-Katha, signifying the belief that every line (geetha) carries an inherent narrative (katha). Envisioned as a platform to explore art that broadens and elevates the viewer’s perspective, Geetha-Katha seeks to reveal the quiet stories embedded in simple visual gestures. Anuradha S.

b: Speaker Hardik Dua is a medical anthropologist, currently working as the Advocacy Officer (Health) at Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy. He has worked on Vidhi’s End-of-Life Care (EOLC) toolkit, co-authored The Queer…
f: Speaker Hardik Dua is a medical anthropologist, currently working as the Advocacy Officer (Health) at Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy. He has worked on Vidhi’s End-of-Life Care (EOLC) toolkit, co-authored The Queer Legacy: An Estate Planning Manual for LGBTQIA+ Individuals (2025). He is currently researching Do-Not-Attempt-Resuscitation (DNAR) orders in India, and serves on the advisory board of QAble.in. Before joining Vidhi, he was Lead-Programs at ETI Services and served on the editorial board of the International Journal of Policy Sciences and Law (IJPSL). He also worked on the assessment of state advocacy and communication strategies on TB for the MoHFW and the Gates Foundation.

b: Speaker Harshita Soni began practising yoga in 2011 to build flexibility, stamina, and strength as a dancer. As the physical pursuit evolved into a profound process of healing and self-discovery, she began teaching yoga…
f: Speaker Harshita Soni began practising yoga in 2011 to build flexibility, stamina, and strength as a dancer. As the physical pursuit evolved into a profound process of healing and self-discovery, she began teaching yoga to make personalized yoga therapy mainstream, and as a means of inner reflection and transformation grounded in Indic psychology. In 2017, she embarked on Vedic chanting to teach healing chants from the Vedas to support her patients. She is a certified Yoga Āchārya, certified Yoga Vaidya, and certified Vedic Chanting Teacher. She also holds a Master’s degree in Engineering, a Diploma in Kuchipudi, and has experience in the field of environment and sustainability.

b: Speaker Haseeb Jafferi , a descendant of the Nizam family, is a cultural curator and experiential educator passionate about Hyderabadi heritage. Founder of ‘Sufi Trails’, he blends history, storytelling, and…
f: Speaker Haseeb Jafferi , a descendant of the Nizam family, is a cultural curator and experiential educator passionate about Hyderabadi heritage. Founder of ‘Sufi Trails’, he blends history, storytelling, and Indo-Persian artistry with leadership expertise, captivating audiences by bringing Hyderabad’s rich legacy to life.

b: Speaker Heena Alam is a spoken word artist who weaves emotions into words that echo through stories and poems, creating an imaginative movie theatre. She has performed at multiple open mics, curated shows, and…
f: Speaker Heena Alam is a spoken word artist who weaves emotions into words that echo through stories and poems, creating an imaginative movie theatre. She has performed at multiple open mics, curated shows, and literature festivals, including at IFP Season 15, New Delhi, Fringe Festival, Samvidhan Mahotsav, IIT Roorkee Thomso 2025, Sahitya Tak, Satyawati College, and Jashn-e-Adab. She won the annual open mic competition of the My City My Voice platform in 2025.

b: Speaker Hisham Mundol is Chief Advisor in India to the Environmental Defense Fund (EDF), in which role he leads the organization’s strategy centering on supporting an Indian pathway to shared sustainable prosperity.…
f: Speaker Hisham Mundol is Chief Advisor in India to the Environmental Defense Fund (EDF), in which role he leads the organization’s strategy centering on supporting an Indian pathway to shared sustainable prosperity. EDF’s priorities are demonstrating the viability of sustainable livelihoods, partnering to demonstrate shareholder value creation through responsible business, building market-based mechanisms to further climate progress, as well as catalyzing the climate tech ecosystem in India. He led the work of the Children’s Investment Fund Foundation in India and also ran the National Condoms Programme for the Indian Government’s National AIDS Control Organization, and later set up operations in South Asia for Wikimedia Foundation, promoting projects like Wikipedia.

b: Speaker Indu Chinta documents and preserves cultural heritage through publications and photographs. She has been researching into theyyam, a traditional expression of religious worship in Kerala, and has documented more…
f: Speaker Indu Chinta documents and preserves cultural heritage through publications and photographs. She has been researching into theyyam, a traditional expression of religious worship in Kerala, and has documented more than a hundred theyyams through photographs. Her work won the Kerala government’s Kerala Folklore Academy Award in 2020. Her books include Theyyam: Merging with the Divine (2018) and Iconography of Deepam: Traditional Lamps of Kerala (2023). She has a Master’s in Environmental Engineering from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, and worked with policy think-tanks in India, on the United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development (UNCSD), and was associated with the first edition of Carbon Zero Challenge at IIT Madras.

b: Speaker Inez Baranay was born in Italy of Hungarian parents, is an English language writer of Australian citizenship, a refugee background, transnational culture, and cosmopolitan temperament. In the 1980s, she began…
f: Speaker Inez Baranay was born in Italy of Hungarian parents, is an English language writer of Australian citizenship, a refugee background, transnational culture, and cosmopolitan temperament. In the 1980s, she began publishing short fiction in small press anthologies. Her essays and stories have since been published in a range of journals and anthologies. Soul Climate (2025) is her tenth novel. Neem Dreams (2003) and With the Tiger (2008) were also first published in India. She has taught creative writing in various contexts and been a guest at conferences, seminars, literature festivals, and international writers’ centres.

b: Speaker Inga Marie Ramcke is a science educator based in Hamburg, Germany. She is a member of the children’s book writer network Elbautoren and focuses on non-fiction. Her books are published by German, Danish, and…
f: Speaker Inga Marie Ramcke is a science educator based in Hamburg, Germany. She is a member of the children’s book writer network Elbautoren and focuses on non-fiction. Her books are published by German, Danish, and Russian publishing houses. Through the science communication project Plötzlich Wissen!, she also works with adult audiences. Across both areas, she uses puppeteering to engage audiences of all ages with sustainable development topics. Her books cover space science, biology, and physics, while her adult work focuses on seas and oceans, combining playfulness, interaction, humour, and accessibility. Her approach encourages curiosity, dialogue, creativity, empathy, understanding, and scientific engagement.

b: Speaker Ipsita Chakravarty is an award-winning journalist who has reported on politics and armed conflict in Kashmir and North-East India for a decade. She has worked as a reporter, editor, and opinion writer for…
f: Speaker Ipsita Chakravarty is an award-winning journalist who has reported on politics and armed conflict in Kashmir and North-East India for a decade. She has worked as a reporter, editor, and opinion writer for national dailies including The Times of India, The Telegraph, The Indian Express, and Scroll. Her book Dapaan: Tales from Kashmir’s Conflict (2025) has received widespread critical acclaim.

b: Speaker Ismat Mehdi taught French and German in Osmania University and Arabic in EFLU, Hyderabad. She has lectured and written on the history and culture of India and the Middle East, Sufiism, Women in Islam, Mahatma…
f: Speaker Ismat Mehdi taught French and German in Osmania University and Arabic in EFLU, Hyderabad. She has lectured and written on the history and culture of India and the Middle East, Sufiism, Women in Islam, Mahatma Gandhi, and Hyderabad. She has been a Supervisor of the Arabic Service of All India Radio, New Delhi, and Director of Maulana Azad Cultural Centre, Indian Embassy, Cairo. Her recent books include Abid Hasan Safrani: Netaji’s Comrade in Arms (2023) and her memoir I Almost Wasn’t (2025). She is a recipient of the President of India’s award for scholarship in Arabic.

b: Speaker Ita Mehrotra is a visual artist, researcher, and educator. She creates non-fiction comics, graphic narratives, and illustrated texts, with a focus on citizenship rights, displacement, and witness-based memory…
f: Speaker Ita Mehrotra is a visual artist, researcher, and educator. She creates non-fiction comics, graphic narratives, and illustrated texts, with a focus on citizenship rights, displacement, and witness-based memory keeping from a feminist lens. Her graphic books include Uprooted: A Graphic Account of the Struggle for Forest Rights (2025) and Shaheen Bagh: A Graphic Recollection (2021). She has published and exhibited her work widely over the past decade and received grant awards from national and international organizations. She has an MPhil from the School of Arts and Aesthetics, JNU, and is a visiting faculty at Ashoka University. She leads visual art programmes with rural schools and libraries across India.

b: Speaker Jaideep Unudurti is a freelance journalist who writes on travel and books for leading Indian publications. His WW1-themed graphic novel Die Unterirdischen Städte , with artist Fabian Stoltz, was published in…
f: Speaker Jaideep Unudurti is a freelance journalist who writes on travel and books for leading Indian publications. His WW1-themed graphic novel Die Unterirdischen Städte , with artist Fabian Stoltz, was published in 2019. Along with artist Harsho, he is now working on Lovecraft in India , set in 1930s Calcutta and featuring an occult narrative. He also developed “Every City is a Story”—a city-centric graphic storytelling initiative encompassing various cities in India. The project began as an oral history initiative in the Old City of Hyderabad and encompassed archival research, photography, and lots of impromptu conversations with passers-by in Irani cafes.

b: Speaker Poetry and pathos often complement each other, and for Jameela Nishat, it is easy to see where she finds her inspiration. To rescue young girls and women from abusive environments and the clutches of patriarchy…
f: Speaker Poetry and pathos often complement each other, and for Jameela Nishat, it is easy to see where she finds her inspiration. To rescue young girls and women from abusive environments and the clutches of patriarchy has been the focus of her organisation ‘Shaheen Women’s Resource and Welfare Association’, established in 2002. The life stories of these women inspired Ms. Nishat to bring to the world the intensity of their anguish through her poetry and social work. Recipient of several awards (Devi Award, 2015; Ladli Award 2012; Govt. of Andhra Pradesh award for promoting Deccani language 2007), this is her fourth volume of poetry in translation apart from two in Urdu.

b: Speaker Jayachandran Surendran is a dance practitioner and Lecturer at the Centre for Exact Humanities, IIIT Hyderabad, focusing on the formal nature of art. An Electronics Engineer- turned-artist, he previously worked…
f: Speaker Jayachandran Surendran is a dance practitioner and Lecturer at the Centre for Exact Humanities, IIIT Hyderabad, focusing on the formal nature of art. An Electronics Engineer- turned-artist, he previously worked with Wipro and later at Kalakshetra Foundation as an Assistant Professor. Trained under eminent gurus, including Smt. Leela Samson and Prof. C.V. Chandrasekhar, he holds multiple postgraduate degrees and a PhD in Dance. His research on universal dance fundamentals led to India’s first patented dance teaching tool. A performer, choreographer, and scholar, he is widely recognized for his lectures, writings, and studies on temple architecture and choreography.

b: Speaker Jhansi Laxmi is an actor and anchor by profession with three decades of experience and nine Nandi Awards. She is also a playwright, director, and theater practitioner by passion, and a media activist who works…
f: Speaker Jhansi Laxmi is an actor and anchor by profession with three decades of experience and nine Nandi Awards. She is also a playwright, director, and theater practitioner by passion, and a media activist who works to raise awareness on gender sensitivity, and an enthusiast for minimalist sustainability.

b: Speaker Jhilam Chattaraj is an academic, critic, and poet. She has authored Sudeep Sen: Reading, Writing, Teaching (2026), Noise Cancellation (2021), Corporate Fiction: Popular Culture and the New Writers (2018), and…
f: Speaker Jhilam Chattaraj is an academic, critic, and poet. She has authored Sudeep Sen: Reading, Writing, Teaching (2026), Noise Cancellation (2021), Corporate Fiction: Popular Culture and the New Writers (2018), and When Lovers Leave and Poetry Stays (2018). Her poem ‘Sari’ was nominated for the Nina Riggs Poetry Award (2023). Her work has been published in Michigan Quarterly Review , Changing Skies , Mekong Review , Ecocene , One Art Poetry Journal , Calyx , Ariel , Colorado Review , World Literature Today , and Asian Cha , among others. She received the CTI Excellence Award in ‘Literature and Soft Skills Development’ (2019) from the Council for Transforming India and the Department of Language and Culture, Government of Telangana.

b: Speaker Jungshi Imti is a content strategist at a marketing agency. He started A Thirdspace Project in 2024 to find community, inspiration, and a catalyst to share life as he lives it. He set up a thrift store in his…
f: Speaker Jungshi Imti is a content strategist at a marketing agency. He started A Thirdspace Project in 2024 to find community, inspiration, and a catalyst to share life as he lives it. He set up a thrift store in his apartment to promote homegrown businesses from Nagaland. Through this initiative, he has brought Naga food to tables around Hyderabad and created a space for people to explore connections. He hopes to take these dinners to places beyond Hyderabad and document stories of how food can help us build a home wherever we go.

b: Speaker Juveria Asif reads, writes, and researches at the intersections of Muslim thought, political philosophy, and Urdu literature. She is also working on her PhD at The EFL University, Hyderabad. N.
f: Speaker Juveria Asif reads, writes, and researches at the intersections of Muslim thought, political philosophy, and Urdu literature. She is also working on her PhD at The EFL University, Hyderabad. N.

b: Speaker Thangaraj is a renowned human geneticist who has made outstanding contributions to our understanding of the complex origins of Indian populations and the impact of endogamy on our health and disease.
f: Speaker Thangaraj is a renowned human geneticist who has made outstanding contributions to our understanding of the complex origins of Indian populations and the impact of endogamy on our health and disease.

b: Speaker Kalpana Karunakaran is an Associate Professor in the Humanities and Social Sciences Department, IIT Madras. Her research and writings are in the domain of gender, labour, microcredit, women’s trade unions, and…
f: Speaker Kalpana Karunakaran is an Associate Professor in the Humanities and Social Sciences Department, IIT Madras. Her research and writings are in the domain of gender, labour, microcredit, women’s trade unions, and solidarity-based movements. She writes about women’s lives with a focus on the intersections of the personal and the political. She is the author of Women, Microfinance and the State in Neo-liberal India (2017), the Tamil memoir, Comrade Amma: Magal Parvaiyil Mythily Sivaraman (Comrade Mother: A Daughter’s Portrait of Mythily Sivaraman; 2018), and A Woman of No Consequence: Memory, Letters and Resistance in Madras (2025).

b: Speaker Kalpana Sinha is the co-founder of The Lit People, a thriving book club in Hyderabad. She is a leadership consultant and coach and is the managing partner of Aaroha: The Humanistic Leadership project, bringing…
f: Speaker Kalpana Sinha is the co-founder of The Lit People, a thriving book club in Hyderabad. She is a leadership consultant and coach and is the managing partner of Aaroha: The Humanistic Leadership project, bringing Indian philosophy to leadership. She worked in senior leadership positions at Microsoft, Accenture, and the McCann World Group in India and overseas. Reading has always been her passion, and founding The Lit People has been her way of creating a movement to get adults back to reading. She is also a watercolour artist trained at the Nanyang School of Fine Arts and has held several exhibitions.

b: Speaker Karthick Narayanan R , a Moturi Satyanarayana Fellow, is a linguist and researcher whose work centres on language documentation, sociolinguistics, and community-led archiving in India. His Multilinguality,…
f: Speaker Karthick Narayanan R , a Moturi Satyanarayana Fellow, is a linguist and researcher whose work centres on language documentation, sociolinguistics, and community-led archiving in India. His Multilinguality, Vitality, and Endangerment: Insights from the Lived Experiences of Multilingual India (2025) draws on long-term fieldwork among the Toda and Kota communities to rethink dominant models of language vitality and displacement. He works at the intersection of multilingualism, language endangerment, and digital infrastructures, designing linguistic archives, developing NLP datasets, and training Indigenous communities to document and govern their languages. His earlier publications include studies on Toda verbal art and language archiving.

b: Speaker Karthik Muralidharan is the Tata Chancellor’s professor of economics at the University of California San Diego (UCSD). His research spans public finance and development Economics, and his publications include…
f: Speaker Karthik Muralidharan is the Tata Chancellor’s professor of economics at the University of California San Diego (UCSD). His research spans public finance and development Economics, and his publications include Accelerating India’s Development: A State-Led Roadmap for Effective Governance (2024) and articles in leading academic journals. He has actively engaged in policy advising and capacity building in India, and in public communication of research insights. He is the co-founder and scientific director of the Centre for Effective Governance of Indian States (CEGIS), a non-profit that works to improve state capacity, governance, and service delivery. He holds a bachelor’s degree and a PhD in economics from Harvard and an MPhil from Cambridge.

b: Speaker Kasturi Mahadik is a scientist with over a decade of experience in biology and holds a PhD focused on how pathogens cause disease. She currently leads the Centre for Predictive Human Model Systems at the Atal…
f: Speaker Kasturi Mahadik is a scientist with over a decade of experience in biology and holds a PhD focused on how pathogens cause disease. She currently leads the Centre for Predictive Human Model Systems at the Atal Incubation Centre–CCMB in Hyderabad. Her work brings advanced technologies into science to help improve how new medicines are discovered.

b: Speaker Kavery Poonacha Nambisan is from Kodagu district, Karnataka. She started writing when she was working as a full-fledged surgeon in remote parts of Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka. She has written…
f: Speaker Kavery Poonacha Nambisan is from Kodagu district, Karnataka. She started writing when she was working as a full-fledged surgeon in remote parts of Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka. She has written eight novels, two non-fiction books, and several essays, both medical and literary. Several of her novels have been shortlisted for major literary awards. Her most recent publication is Rising Sons: A Novel (2025).

b: Speaker Kavita Kané is the author of nine novels based on lesser-known women in Indian mythology: Karna’s Wife (2013), Sita’s Sister (2014), Menaka’s Choice (2015), Lanka’s Princess (2016), The Fisher Queen’s Dynasty…
f: Speaker Kavita Kané is the author of nine novels based on lesser-known women in Indian mythology: Karna’s Wife (2013), Sita’s Sister (2014), Menaka’s Choice (2015), Lanka’s Princess (2016), The Fisher Queen’s Dynasty (2017), Ahalya’s Awakening (2019), Sarasvati’s Gift (2021), Tara’s Truce (2023), and the latest, Bhima’s Wife (2025) . She has postgraduate degrees from the University of Pune in English Literature and Mass Communication and Journalism. After two decades with Magna Publishing and DNA, she became a full-time author.

b: Speaker Kazim Ali is the author of numerous books of poetry, fiction, essays, and cross-genre work. Sukun: New and Selected Poems (2023) is his recent poetry book , Indian Winter (2024), his recent novel , and Black…
f: Speaker Kazim Ali is the author of numerous books of poetry, fiction, essays, and cross-genre work. Sukun: New and Selected Poems (2023) is his recent poetry book , Indian Winter (2024), his recent novel , and Black Buffalo Woman: An Introduction to the Poetry and Poetics of Lucille Clifton (2024) , which won the Poetry Foundation’s Pegagus Award for Criticism, his recent book of nonfiction. He co-founded Nightboat Books in 2004 and served as the press’s first publisher. He currently serves as Professor of Comparative Literature and Literary Arts, and Associate Director of the Institute for Arts and Humanities at the University of California, San Diego.

b: Speaker Keerthana Swaminathan is a sports psychologist and co-director of ‘The Performance Doctor’, a multidisciplinary sports clinic in Chennai. She has a Master’s in Sports and Exercise Psychology from Loughborough…
f: Speaker Keerthana Swaminathan is a sports psychologist and co-director of ‘The Performance Doctor’, a multidisciplinary sports clinic in Chennai. She has a Master’s in Sports and Exercise Psychology from Loughborough University, and is pursuing her PhD from the University of Staffordshire. She assists sportspersons, athletes, and teams to cultivate mental and emotional attributes essential for achieving excellence in their discipline. As the president of the Indian Sports Psychologists Association (INSPA), she works to develop and promote culturally competent and ethically sound practices among aspiring students and established sports psychologists. She leads Project CARE, an INSPA initiative dedicated to promoting Athlete Mental Health Literacy and Psychological First Aid. Usha Raman Festival Director Rekha Bhatnagar Speaker Lalgudi GJR Krishnan Speaker

b: Speaker Kesar Khinvasara is a multidisciplinary abstract artist. Over the years, her need to communicate evolved into a rich, intuitive practice. Her work is marked by a fascination with intricate motifs, bold lines,…
f: Speaker Kesar Khinvasara is a multidisciplinary abstract artist. Over the years, her need to communicate evolved into a rich, intuitive practice. Her work is marked by a fascination with intricate motifs, bold lines, and vibrant colors, resulting in an ever-expanding visual vocabulary. Her academic background in philosophy further informs her practice, enriching her inquiry into perception, memory, form, and color. Her work has been exhibited internationally. She has illustrated two coloring books, both of which have been published in expanded and translated editions. She has participated in two editions of an art festival in India and had the opportunity to contribute to the development of a museum project.

b: Speaker KP Jayasankar , former Professor, School of Media and Cultural Studies, Tata Institute of Social Sciences, Mumbai, is involved in documentary production, teaching, and research. He has been a commissioning…
f: Speaker KP Jayasankar , former Professor, School of Media and Cultural Studies, Tata Institute of Social Sciences, Mumbai, is involved in documentary production, teaching, and research. He has been a commissioning editor and mentor for over 100 documentaries by students and early-career filmmakers. He received the Satish Bahadur Lifetime Achievement Award for Excellence in Film Education from the National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad (2022). He was an invited artist at the Kochi-Muziris Biennale 2018, where “Saacha” (The Loom) was showcased as an installation. His co-authored book A Fly in the Curry (2016), on independent Indian documentary, got a Special Mention for the best book on cinema at the National Film Awards 2016.

b: Speaker Lahari Surapaneni is a senior nutritionist based in Hyderabad and the founder of Nutriful You, a nutrition and wellness clinic. She holds a bachelor’s degree in Food Technology from Osmania University and a PhD…
f: Speaker Lahari Surapaneni is a senior nutritionist based in Hyderabad and the founder of Nutriful You, a nutrition and wellness clinic. She holds a bachelor’s degree in Food Technology from Osmania University and a PhD in Food Science and Nutrition from Clemson University, USA, with postdoctoral research experience at Penn State University. With over 15 years of experience as a researcher, lecturer, and consultant, she specializes in evidence-based, sustainable nutrition. A certified diabetes educator, lactation counselor, and fitness trainer, she also works closely with amateur athletes on performance nutrition. An avid runner herself, she regularly trains and participates in half marathons. Vijay Kumar Tadakamalla Festival Director Daneesh Majid Speaker N.

b: Speaker Lalgudi GJR Krishnan . In 1965, an Italian violin arrived at our home when I was five. That marked the beginning of a lifelong fascination with sound and craftsmanship. That same year, my father and Guru brought…
f: Speaker Lalgudi GJR Krishnan . In 1965, an Italian violin arrived at our home when I was five. That marked the beginning of a lifelong fascination with sound and craftsmanship. That same year, my father and Guru brought home the legendary Papa Venkatramiah’s violin, repaired in London. Years later, I met master luthier James Wimmer and invited him to India for a 21-day workshop through the Lalgudi Trust. Despite initial hesitation, we trained local craftsmen, gifted tools, and instilled precision and passion. By 2019, four Stradivarius replicas were created. Today, these luthiers, including India’s first woman luthier, serve top professionals, leaving a growing legacy for India and beyond.

b: Speaker Lalitha Krishnan is a certified dog trainer, potter, and podcaster who works from her hillside home in Ranikhet, nestled in the Indian Himalaya. She spends much of her day in the garden on the edge of the…
f: Speaker Lalitha Krishnan is a certified dog trainer, potter, and podcaster who works from her hillside home in Ranikhet, nestled in the Indian Himalaya. She spends much of her day in the garden on the edge of the forest—observing, documenting, and delighting in the full spectrum of nature’s Offerings. The Stray Dogs of Landour Network: A True Story by a Failed Dog Trainer (2025) is her debut publication.

b: Speaker ‘ Laltu ’ (Harjinder Singh) is a poet and author writing in Hindi. A recipient of Siya Sahachari Samman of Sahitya Garima Puraskar, Hyderabad, he has published a dozen anthologies of poetry and two books of…
f: Speaker ‘ Laltu ’ (Harjinder Singh) is a poet and author writing in Hindi. A recipient of Siya Sahachari Samman of Sahitya Garima Puraskar, Hyderabad, he has published a dozen anthologies of poetry and two books of short stories. His works have been translated into several languages, including English. He has also written for children and neo-literates. He teaches science and literature, and is a professor emeritus at IIIT-Hyderabad.

b: Speaker Lateef Ahmad Lone is an Arts Graduate from Government Degree College, Gurez, Jammu and Kashmir.
f: Speaker Lateef Ahmad Lone is an Arts Graduate from Government Degree College, Gurez, Jammu and Kashmir.

b: Speaker Laura Spinney is a writer and science journalist. Her writing on science has appeared in The Guardian, The Economist, Nature , and National Geographic , among others. She is the author of two novels, The Doctor…
f: Speaker Laura Spinney is a writer and science journalist. Her writing on science has appeared in The Guardian, The Economist, Nature , and National Geographic , among others. She is the author of two novels, The Doctor (2001) and The Quick (2007), and a collection of oral history, Rue Centrale (2013). Her bestselling non-fiction account of the 1918 flu pandemic, Pale Rider: The Spanish Flu of 1918 and How it Changed the World (2017), was translated into more than 20 languages. Her latest book, Proto: How Once Ancient Language Went Global (2025) is the story of the Indo-European languages. She lives in Paris.

b: Speaker Luvlina Bhardwaj has been a Corporate Training Consultant with IT companies in Hyderabad for 13 years. A gold medalist in PG in Psychological Counseling Skills and Past Director and senior volunteer for 27 years…
f: Speaker Luvlina Bhardwaj has been a Corporate Training Consultant with IT companies in Hyderabad for 13 years. A gold medalist in PG in Psychological Counseling Skills and Past Director and senior volunteer for 27 years with Roshni, an NGO that provides free confidential emotional support for the depressed and suicidal. She is also the Founder Member of ‘Break the Silence’, a citizens’ initiative working for child safety.

b: Speaker M. A. Aleem is an engineer with a master’s in business administration. He loves languages and calligraphy, and is a Fellow at Anveshi, Research Centre for Women’s Studies, Hyderabad. He is currently researching…
f: Speaker M. A. Aleem is an engineer with a master’s in business administration. He loves languages and calligraphy, and is a Fellow at Anveshi, Research Centre for Women’s Studies, Hyderabad. He is currently researching the Urdu public sphere in Hyderabad.

b: Speaker M.A. Moid is a Research Fellow at Anveshi Research Centre for Women’s Studies. His research interests include the culture, history, and politics of contemporary Hyderabad. He has a Ph.D. from the Centre for…
f: Speaker M.A. Moid is a Research Fellow at Anveshi Research Centre for Women’s Studies. His research interests include the culture, history, and politics of contemporary Hyderabad. He has a Ph.D. from the Centre for Social Exclusion in MANUU.

b: Speaker Mahua Sen is an author, editor, and translator. She recently published The Dead Fish (2025), an English translation of Rajkamal Chaudhary’s Hindi novel Machhli mari hui . Her poetry book, Nostalgia Crafting a…
f: Speaker Mahua Sen is an author, editor, and translator. She recently published The Dead Fish (2025), an English translation of Rajkamal Chaudhary’s Hindi novel Machhli mari hui . Her poetry book, Nostalgia Crafting a Home Within (2023), won the prestigious Maharshi Ved Vyas International Award (2024) and was also shortlisted for the Banaras Lit Fest Award (2025). She has co-authored more than 70 books, edited three anthologies, and written essays, articles, short stories, and poetry for national and international ezines and newspapers.

b: Speaker Mamang Dai is a poet and novelist. A Member of Arunachal Pradesh Public Service Commission (2011-2017), a former journalist and President of the Arunachal Pradesh Union of Working Journalists, she worked with…
f: Speaker Mamang Dai is a poet and novelist. A Member of Arunachal Pradesh Public Service Commission (2011-2017), a former journalist and President of the Arunachal Pradesh Union of Working Journalists, she worked with the World Wide Fund for Nature in the Eastern Himalaya Biodiversity Hotspots programme. Her first book, Arunachal Pradesh: The Hidden Land , featuring the culture and customs of the state’s communities, won the State Verrier Elwin Award (2023). A Padma Shri awardee (2011), she received the Sahitya Akademi Award (2017) for her novel The Black Hill . Her recent publications include The White Shirts of Summer (poetry, 2023) and The Inheritance of Words: Writings from Arunachal Pradesh (2024).

b: Speaker Manish Saksena is a lifestyle specialist with over 31 years of experience across product, brand management, design, marketing, visual merchandising, and retail operations. He has contributed to the entry of…
f: Speaker Manish Saksena is a lifestyle specialist with over 31 years of experience across product, brand management, design, marketing, visual merchandising, and retail operations. He has contributed to the entry of international brands into India and the creation of successful homegrown labels. As COO of Tommy Hilfiger India, he led the brand’s growth and profitability before co-founding LimeRoad and consulting for Amazon. Passionate about craft, he now leads Aadyam Handwoven, driving revenue and social impact for weavers across key clusters. He mentors craft-led startups and advises global brands. An alumnus of St. Stephen’s College and London College of Fashion, he remains deeply engaged with textiles, arts, and culture.

b: Speaker Manisha Sobhrajani works with communities in remote and hostile environments across India, focusing on trauma, reconciliation, and the human cost of conflict and displacement. With a background in journalism and…
f: Speaker Manisha Sobhrajani works with communities in remote and hostile environments across India, focusing on trauma, reconciliation, and the human cost of conflict and displacement. With a background in journalism and publishing, she combines rigorous research and a deep commitment to lived realities in her fieldwork and writing, amplifying voices often excluded from mainstream narratives. Her work engages with grassroots groups, policymakers, and scholars, bridging gaps between on-the-ground realities and broader discourses of justice and human rights. The Land I Dream Of: The Story of Kashmir’s Women (2014) was her first book, and Shadows of Azadi: Women’s Lives in the Crucible of Kashmir (2025) is her latest edited volume of essays.

b: Speaker Manjiri Prabhu is an award-winning international author of 23 books, a short-film-maker, and the Curator and Founder/Director of Pune International Literary Festival and International Festival of Spiritual India…
f: Speaker Manjiri Prabhu is an award-winning international author of 23 books, a short-film-maker, and the Curator and Founder/Director of Pune International Literary Festival and International Festival of Spiritual India (for Humanity & Wisdom). The first female mystery author to be published outside India, she has completed 52 years in the world of writing. Her book The Rampur Raza Mystery: A Sassy Library Thriller (2023) was launched by the Hon. President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu. She has been invited to many reputed international literature festivals like The Oxford Literary Festival, Frankfurt Book Fair, and Jaipur Literature Festival.

b: Speaker Mehak Jamal is a filmmaker and author from Kashmir. She is a 2022 South Asia Speaks Fellow, awarded to outstanding emerging writers from the region. Her film Bad Egg premiered at the 19th Indian Film Festival…
f: Speaker Mehak Jamal is a filmmaker and author from Kashmir. She is a 2022 South Asia Speaks Fellow, awarded to outstanding emerging writers from the region. Her film Bad Egg premiered at the 19th Indian Film Festival Stuttgart and won the Audience Award. It was screened at and won awards at multiple film festivals, including Melbourne, Madrid, Chicago, Atlanta, Washington DC, Kerala, Bangalore, and Dharamshala. She is a film alumna of Srishti Institute of Art, Design and Technology, Bangalore. Lōal Kashmir : Love and Longing in a Torn Land (2025) is her first book.

b: Speaker MK Raina is an actor, director, filmmaker, and academic. He is a major contributor to Indian New Wave cinema and is instrumental in reviving ‘Bhand Pather’, the traditional folk theatre of Kashmir. He received…
f: Speaker MK Raina is an actor, director, filmmaker, and academic. He is a major contributor to Indian New Wave cinema and is instrumental in reviving ‘Bhand Pather’, the traditional folk theatre of Kashmir. He received several honours, including the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, the BV Karanth Lifetime Achievement Award, and has been a visiting faculty at several institutions, including the National School of Drama, and is currently an Artist-in-Residence at IIT Gandhinagar. He has also been a Fellow at Stanford University and a Scholar-in-Residence at Jamia Millia Islamia. Before I Forget: A Memoir (2024) chronicles his life, career, and activism against the backdrop of major social and political changes in India.

b: Speaker Mo Naga (MoranngamKhaling) is an ethnic Uipo Naga tattoo artist. Originally from Manipur, he trained as a fashion designer at the National Institute of Fashion Technology, Hyderabad, where he started tattooing…
f: Speaker Mo Naga (MoranngamKhaling) is an ethnic Uipo Naga tattoo artist. Originally from Manipur, he trained as a fashion designer at the National Institute of Fashion Technology, Hyderabad, where he started tattooing fifteen years ago. Over the course of his career, he has become recognized as one of India’s most prominent tattoo artists. He was one of only three India-based artists featured in The World Atlas of Tattoo (2015), which chronicles the work of one hundred leading global tattooists.

b: Speaker Mohammed Ishak Ziaee has been a career consultant with Deloitte Consulting till he retired in 2015. He formed the Hyderabad chapter of Urban Sketchers Hyderabad (USk Hyd) in 2017, with the concept of like-minded…
f: Speaker Mohammed Ishak Ziaee has been a career consultant with Deloitte Consulting till he retired in 2015. He formed the Hyderabad chapter of Urban Sketchers Hyderabad (USk Hyd) in 2017, with the concept of like-minded individuals coming together with a passion for sketching and drawing in a live environment. He now balances life between freelance consulting, managing Urban Sketchers along with a great team, occasional watercolour plein air stints, and mentoring and advising young artists.
