b: Speaker Mohammed Khadeer Babu is a well-known Telugu writer, editor, anthologist, and scriptwriter. His early collections of childhood stories— Dargamitta Kathalu & Poleramma Banda Kathalu (2016) continue to enthral…
f: Speaker Mohammed Khadeer Babu is a well-known Telugu writer, editor, anthologist, and scriptwriter. His early collections of childhood stories— Dargamitta Kathalu & Poleramma Banda Kathalu (2016) continue to enthral readers. The stories “Head Curry” and “Three-fourths”, Half Price”, and “Bajji Bajji” have been translated into English, Hindi, and Urdu as part of the “Different Tales” Series published by Anveshi Hyderabad and Ekalavya Publishers. That’s A Fire Ant Right There! Tales From Kavali (2025) is the latest translation of his stories.

b: Speaker Mohd Abdul Nayeem teaches Organizational Behavior, Business Management, and Social Sciences at ICFAI Business School, Hyderabad. A die-hard movie enthusiast, he volunteers at Lamakaan and curates the Wednesday…
f: Speaker Mohd Abdul Nayeem teaches Organizational Behavior, Business Management, and Social Sciences at ICFAI Business School, Hyderabad. A die-hard movie enthusiast, he volunteers at Lamakaan and curates the Wednesday Film screenings there. Whether watching films or diving into fiction, he values the power of stories to connect people and evoke profound emotions. He actively participates in socio-cultural events in Hyderabad and balances academic pursuits with his varied interests and commitments. His love for the Urdu language and literature further enriches his worldview, allowing him to appreciate the elegance of expression and the depth of cultural heritage it embodies.

b: Speaker Mrinalini Shastry is a senior disciple of Guru Smt. Mangala Bhatt and Guru Shri Raghav Raj Bhatt, under whose tutelage she trained in Kathak for over 10 years at Aakruti Kathak Kendra. She is a Doordarshan…
f: Speaker Mrinalini Shastry is a senior disciple of Guru Smt. Mangala Bhatt and Guru Shri Raghav Raj Bhatt, under whose tutelage she trained in Kathak for over 10 years at Aakruti Kathak Kendra. She is a Doordarshan graded artiste and has completed her Diploma in Kathak with distinction. She has performed at several prestigious venues, including Rashtrapati Nilayam, and assisted her Gurus in regular classes and training workshops, including intensive workshops with SPICMACAY. She is an MBA from the Indian School of Business, works on financial inclusion, and is deeply connected to the handloom and handicraft heritage of India.

b: Profile Home > Speakers > Profile C.
f: Profile Home > Speakers > Profile C.

b: Speaker Krishna Reddy is a cardiologist, health systems leader, and global advocate for noncommunicable disease (NCD) prevention and management. As CEO of ACCESS Health International and a member of the Board of…
f: Speaker Krishna Reddy is a cardiologist, health systems leader, and global advocate for noncommunicable disease (NCD) prevention and management. As CEO of ACCESS Health International and a member of the Board of Trustees of the United States Pharmacopeia, he works closely with governments, civil society, and academia across Africa, Asia, and the Middle East to strengthen health systems, advance non-communicable disease programmes, and improve access to affordable, high-quality care. He is a co-founder of Care Hospitals, and also founded Relisys Medical Devices, through which he spearheaded the development of indigenous advanced cardiac device technology, including India’s first coronary stent—the Kalam-Raju stent.

b: Speaker Namita Devidayal is the author of The Music Room (2007 , winner of the 2008 Vodafone Crossword Popular Book Award), Aftertaste (2010), and The Sixth String of Vilayat Khan (2018). She is a journalist with The…
f: Speaker Namita Devidayal is the author of The Music Room (2007 , winner of the 2008 Vodafone Crossword Popular Book Award), Aftertaste (2010), and The Sixth String of Vilayat Khan (2018). She is a journalist with The Times of India . She graduated from Princeton University.

b: Speaker Nancy Adajania is a Bombay-based cultural theorist and curator. She was Joint Artistic Director of the 9th Gwangju Biennale, South Korea (2012). She has curated several exhibitions, including “One Hundred Years…
f: Speaker Nancy Adajania is a Bombay-based cultural theorist and curator. She was Joint Artistic Director of the 9th Gwangju Biennale, South Korea (2012). She has curated several exhibitions, including “One Hundred Years And Counting: Rescripting K G Subramanyan” (Emami with Seagull, 2024) and “Woman Is As Woman Does” (CSMVS Museum with JNAF, 2022). She has proposed several new theoretical models through her extensive writings on subaltern art, media art, public art, collaborative art, transcultural art, and the biennale culture in the Global South.

b: Speaker Nargis Abraham ’s rapport with writing began with a journalism degree and freelance articles in magazines and newspapers. She taught journalistic feature writing at Osmania University in India and professional…
f: Speaker Nargis Abraham ’s rapport with writing began with a journalism degree and freelance articles in magazines and newspapers. She taught journalistic feature writing at Osmania University in India and professional writing skills at BCIT in Burnaby, BC. Along the way, she acquired a PhD and two master’s degrees. Since 2015, she has been a registered member of the Port Moody Writers’ Group, where she has read several of her unpublished short stories and chapters of her novel Munni at my Doorstep (2025).

b: Speaker Nazia Akhtar teaches courses in Indian and Russian literatures at IIIT, Hyderabad. She received grants from the Charles Wallace India Trust and has held fellowships with the New India Foundation and the Akademie…
f: Speaker Nazia Akhtar teaches courses in Indian and Russian literatures at IIIT, Hyderabad. She received grants from the Charles Wallace India Trust and has held fellowships with the New India Foundation and the Akademie Schloss Solitude to write two books on a long tradition of Urdu writing among women in Hyderabad. Her translation of Zeenath Sajida’s Urdu short story “Chhotam Jaan” received a commendation from the jury of the Jawad Memorial Prize (2021). Bibi’s Room: Hyderabadi Women and Twentieth-Century Urdu Prose (2022) was her first book, and her second book, The Deccan Sun: Essays and Stories by Zeenath Sajida (2025), consists of translations of Urdu writings.

b: Speaker Nikhila S is Professor, Department of Film Studies, The EFL University, Hyderabad, where she teaches, researches, and supervises research in the areas of Film Studies and Gender Studies. She has been teaching…
f: Speaker Nikhila S is Professor, Department of Film Studies, The EFL University, Hyderabad, where she teaches, researches, and supervises research in the areas of Film Studies and Gender Studies. She has been teaching for 30 years, including at Mount Carmel College, Bangalore, and Pondicherry University. She has organized seminars, film festivals, and workshops, and presently coordinates an online film discussion forum, “Talking Films Online.” Her recent publications include an article on the narratorial function of the female journalist figure in New Age Kannada Cinema and an article on films on the Chipko Movement for a volume commemorating 50 years of the Movement.

b: Speaker Onir (Anirban Dhar) is an Indian filmmaker, producer, screenwriter, and editor. His film My Brother… Nikhil (2005) was among the first to deal with AIDS and same-sex relationships. His film I Am (2011) was…
f: Speaker Onir (Anirban Dhar) is an Indian filmmaker, producer, screenwriter, and editor. His film My Brother… Nikhil (2005) was among the first to deal with AIDS and same-sex relationships. His film I Am (2011) was adjudged Best Film (Hindi) at the Indian National Film Awards. Its sequel is his latest film, We Are Faheem and Karun (2024). It is the first Kashmiri-language Queer film shot entirely in Kashmir. He received the Rainbow Warrior award for his film Pine Cone (2023). His biography, I Am Onir And I Am Gay (2022), received the Likho award for “Outstanding Book”.

b: Speaker Pamela Philipose , presently the ombudsperson of the New Delhi-based news portal, The Wire.in, has served as editor-in-chief of Women’s Feature Service . Earlier, she was the senior associate editor, The Indian…
f: Speaker Pamela Philipose , presently the ombudsperson of the New Delhi-based news portal, The Wire.in, has served as editor-in-chief of Women’s Feature Service . Earlier, she was the senior associate editor, The Indian Express . She has served as advisor to the Media Task Force of the Government of India’s High Level Status of Women Committee Report. She is the author of Media’s Shifting Terrain: Five Years that Transformed the Way India Communicates (2019), A Boundless Fear Gripped Me: How the Other Half Lived in the Pandemic’s Shadow (2023), and Framing the Media: Government Policies, Law and Freedom of the Press in India (2025). B Kinnera Murthy Festival Director Tejah Balantrapu Festival Director Sneha Banerjee Speaker

b: Speaker Paravasthu Lokeshwar is the author of twenty books, including the trilogy, Salaam Hyderabad (2005), Kallola Kalala Kaalam (2020), and Teeram Cherina Naava (2025), and the collection of stories Charminar Kathalu…
f: Speaker Paravasthu Lokeshwar is the author of twenty books, including the trilogy, Salaam Hyderabad (2005), Kallola Kalala Kaalam (2020), and Teeram Cherina Naava (2025), and the collection of stories Charminar Kathalu (2022) and Sheharnama: The Romance of Hyderabad’s Bastis (2025). He has also published four travelogues, including A Valiant Journey through the Silk Route (2022), two poetry books, Musafir (2002) and Saddam Hussein (2007), and four essay collections on the movement for a separate Telangana state. He travelled widely in Western European countries, England, France, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, China, Bhutan, Australia, and New Zealand.

b: Speaker Paromita Vohra is a filmmaker and writer whose films, online videos, art installations, and television programming explore feminism, gender, desire, urban life, and popular culture. She has directed several…
f: Speaker Paromita Vohra is a filmmaker and writer whose films, online videos, art installations, and television programming explore feminism, gender, desire, urban life, and popular culture. She has directed several documentaries, including Unlimited Girls (2022), Q2P (2006), Where’s Sandra? (2005), Morality TV and the Loving Jehad (2007), Partners in Crime (2011), and Working Girls (2025). She has written the film Khamosh Pani/Silent Waters (2003), the comic Priya’s Mirror (2016), and the play Ishqiya Dharavi Ishtyle . In 2015, she founded Agents of Ishq, a pioneering digital platform which has transformed conversations on sex, love, and desire in India. Her weekly column in Sunday Midday is currently in its 15th year.

b: Speaker Pawan Toppo is Assistant Professor of English at Sukanta Mahavidyalaya, West Bengal. His doctoral work is on the Oraon/Kurukh festivals of the Dooars region. His research interests include Adivasi Studies, Folk…
f: Speaker Pawan Toppo is Assistant Professor of English at Sukanta Mahavidyalaya, West Bengal. His doctoral work is on the Oraon/Kurukh festivals of the Dooars region. His research interests include Adivasi Studies, Folk Studies, New Critical Humanities, and Film Studies. His documentary Becoming Adivasi: Oraon/Kurukh Festivals of the Dooars Region (2024) explores the rearticulation of Adivasi identity through cultural performances. The film was screened at the 6th Baripada National Indigenous Short Film Festival 2024.

b: Speaker Peggy Mohan was born in Trinidad, West Indies, studied linguistics at the University of the West Indies, and completed her PhD in linguistics from the University of Michigan (1978). She has taught linguistics at…
f: Speaker Peggy Mohan was born in Trinidad, West Indies, studied linguistics at the University of the West Indies, and completed her PhD in linguistics from the University of Michigan (1978). She has taught linguistics at Howard University, Washington D.C., Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Ashoka University, and mass communications at Jamia Millia Islamia, New Delhi. She is the author of three novels, Jahajin (2008), The Youngest Suspect (2012), and Walk in C Minor (2015), and the non-fiction books Wanderers, Kings, Merchants (2021), which won the Mathrubhumi Book of the Year Award, and Father Tongue, Motherland (2025). She lives in New Delhi.

b: Speaker Phejin Konyak is the author of the award-winning book The Konyaks: Last of the Tattooed Headhunters (2017). It was released by Shri Ramnath Kovind, President of India, on 1 December 2017, at Kisama Heritage…
f: Speaker Phejin Konyak is the author of the award-winning book The Konyaks: Last of the Tattooed Headhunters (2017). It was released by Shri Ramnath Kovind, President of India, on 1 December 2017, at Kisama Heritage Village during the Hornbill Festival. The book is an outcome of nearly four years of intensive research work documenting the vanishing tattoo tradition of the Konyak tribe in India and Myanmar.

b: Speaker Pingle Pranav Reddy is the visionary force behind Mirage Media, one of India’s youngest and most fearless production houses delivering back-to-back commercial and critical successes on OTT platforms. As a…
f: Speaker Pingle Pranav Reddy is the visionary force behind Mirage Media, one of India’s youngest and most fearless production houses delivering back-to-back commercial and critical successes on OTT platforms. As a filmmaker, producer, and creative curator, he stands at the intersection of cinema, activism, and heritage, telling stories that challenge power, ignite discourse, and spotlight voices often left unheard.

b: Speaker Ponnari Gottipati is a research management professional and Associate Director – Research at the LV Prasad Eye Institute, Hyderabad, whose work focuses on strengthening research systems and practices. Trained in…
f: Speaker Ponnari Gottipati is a research management professional and Associate Director – Research at the LV Prasad Eye Institute, Hyderabad, whose work focuses on strengthening research systems and practices. Trained in life sciences, she holds a PhD from the University of Sheffield and completed her postdoctoral work at the University of Oxford, UK. She is a recipient of the India Research Management Initiative award, recognised as an Emerging Leader under the IVLP programme of the US Department of State, and a current WomenLift Health India Fellow. A science outreach enthusiast, she co-founded the Superheroes Against Superbugs initiative to raise awareness on the global health threat of antimicrobial resistance.

b: Speaker Pooja Sampath is an Executive Producer, Filmmaker, and Creative. She is a former Executive Producer at Network18, and worked on a documentary series for CNA Insider (Singapore), We don’t play Dolly , which was…
f: Speaker Pooja Sampath is an Executive Producer, Filmmaker, and Creative. She is a former Executive Producer at Network18, and worked on a documentary series for CNA Insider (Singapore), We don’t play Dolly , which was nominated at the Cannes MIPCOM Diversify TV awards (2022). Her independently produced fiction short “Notary” won laurels at The Independent Short Awards, LA (2019 and 2022), and at other film festivals. She has worked as a VFX Production Manager at a studio in Germany. She shifted to documentary productions, telling stories of the natural world. She is working on a documentary on seed-saving practices in India, and a film on the lives of a coastal community.

b: Speaker Potturu Ranganayakulu , an expert in Ayurveda and the history of medicine with a PhD in archaeology, previously compiled the Sanskrit-English Ayurveda Dictionary and the Esperanto-English Dictionary. Since 2018,…
f: Speaker Potturu Ranganayakulu , an expert in Ayurveda and the history of medicine with a PhD in archaeology, previously compiled the Sanskrit-English Ayurveda Dictionary and the Esperanto-English Dictionary. Since 2018, he has led the dictionary department at the Ramoji Foundation, culminating in 2025 with the publication of two massive dictionaries containing 219,000 headwords across six volumes.

b: Speaker Pranav Johri is a multidrug-resistant infection survivor. After struggling with his MDR infection and multiple failed antibiotic treatments, he found a successful treatment in the form of phage therapy for his…
f: Speaker Pranav Johri is a multidrug-resistant infection survivor. After struggling with his MDR infection and multiple failed antibiotic treatments, he found a successful treatment in the form of phage therapy for his infection. His experience led him to found Vitalis Phage Therapy, an initiative with the mission of spreading awareness of the problem of Antimicrobial Resistance ( AMR) and of phage therapy as a solution to the problem. In its 7 years of existence, Vitalis Phage Therapy has enabled phage therapy treatments for over 320 patients in India suffering from multidrug and extensively drug-resistant infections.

b: Speaker Pratima Jaidev is a writer, filmmaker, and CEO of Tarangini Media Works, a legacy production company founded by her father. With over two decades of experience across media, corporate, and education sectors in…
f: Speaker Pratima Jaidev is a writer, filmmaker, and CEO of Tarangini Media Works, a legacy production company founded by her father. With over two decades of experience across media, corporate, and education sectors in India and the U.S., she has created 100+ films spanning documentaries, commercials, and short stories. Her anthology True Spirit (2025) marks her literary debut. She also co-founded Creative Aspirations, an overseas education consultancy firm guiding students into global creative careers.

b: Speaker Prince Azmet Jah , Asaf Jah IX, ascended the gaddi in January 2023 as the titular Nizam of Hyderabad. He is the eldest son of H.E.H. Mukarram Jah and succeeded his father in accordance with the late Nizam’s…
f: Speaker Prince Azmet Jah , Asaf Jah IX, ascended the gaddi in January 2023 as the titular Nizam of Hyderabad. He is the eldest son of H.E.H. Mukarram Jah and succeeded his father in accordance with the late Nizam’s wishes. He is the eldest great-grandchild of the seventh Nizam of Hyderabad. Born in London, he spent his formative years in Hyderabad. He completed a BA in cinematography from the University of Southern California, pursued a career in films, and worked as an assistant cameraman with notable filmmakers on several blockbuster films. He oversees the various trusts set up by his late father, including the Chowmahala Palace Trust.

b: Speaker Priya Thiagarajan sits at the unique intersection of literary tradition and digital learning innovation. While professionally driving global learning strategies using AI and immersive technologies for over two…
f: Speaker Priya Thiagarajan sits at the unique intersection of literary tradition and digital learning innovation. While professionally driving global learning strategies using AI and immersive technologies for over two decades, her personal landscape is shaped by an abiding passion for poetry spanning English, Tamil, and Hindi. This duality allows her to approach poetry with both analytical depth and profound artistic appreciation for verse. She is driven by a philosophy of continuous curiosity—learning, unlearning, and relearning—to understand the evolving shapes of modern poetry.

b: Speaker Priyadarshini Panchapakesan is a children’s author, teacher, and storyteller. Her books, The Myth of the Wild Gaur (2023) and The Guardians of the Forest (2023), blend adventure with environmental themes,…
f: Speaker Priyadarshini Panchapakesan is a children’s author, teacher, and storyteller. Her books, The Myth of the Wild Gaur (2023) and The Guardians of the Forest (2023), blend adventure with environmental themes, inspiring young readers to care for their homes. Her books celebrate the Western Ghats while addressing the challenges of deforestation, climate change, and tourism. She is an experienced educator who conducts storytelling and creative writing workshops to help young readers see the natural world with curiosity and care.

b: Speaker Priyasha Choudhary is a researcher exploring the intersections of disability, gender, sexuality, and care in India. She has worked as a research assistant/associate at the University of Amsterdam and IIT…
f: Speaker Priyasha Choudhary is a researcher exploring the intersections of disability, gender, sexuality, and care in India. She has worked as a research assistant/associate at the University of Amsterdam and IIT Hyderabad, contributing to projects on intellectual disability, gender, and long-term care. Trained in core social sciences, she draws on critical disability studies, medical anthropology, kinship, and feminist ethnography to examine how ableism and patriarchy shape care and kinship. With strong feminist underpinnings, her research is guided by critical and rights-based perspectives, centering lived experiences and feminist methodologies.

b: Speaker Rachita Taneja is a political cartoonist and the creator of ‘Sanitary Panels’, a feminist webcomic that comments on society, culture, and politics. Through her work, she observes the mood of the country on…
f: Speaker Rachita Taneja is a political cartoonist and the creator of ‘Sanitary Panels’, a feminist webcomic that comments on society, culture, and politics. Through her work, she observes the mood of the country on politics and current affairs, and aims to challenge myths and taboos around menstruation, mental health, and queer rights.

b: Speaker Radhika Krishnan is an Associate Professor with the Human Sciences Research Centre at IIIT Hyderabad. Her book Shankar Guha Niyogi: A Politics in Red and Green (2025) looks at the alternative ecological and…
f: Speaker Radhika Krishnan is an Associate Professor with the Human Sciences Research Centre at IIIT Hyderabad. Her book Shankar Guha Niyogi: A Politics in Red and Green (2025) looks at the alternative ecological and technological imaginations emerging from the mines and factory floor in Chhattisgarh, India. Most recently, she has been working on multiple projects on the possibilities of a just transition away from coal in India.

b: Speaker Rahil Mohsin is a visual artist specialising in sequential storytelling. He is an active voice in India’s thriving indie comics scene. His portfolio features work with Scout Comics, Action Lab Studio, Sliced…
f: Speaker Rahil Mohsin is a visual artist specialising in sequential storytelling. He is an active voice in India’s thriving indie comics scene. His portfolio features work with Scout Comics, Action Lab Studio, Sliced Quarterly, Comixense, Scholastic, among others, and four self-published titles. Raised in a Dakhni-speaking household, he rarely saw his language represented in comics or animation and set out to change that. With his partner Alankrita Amaya, he co-founded Hallubol, a comics initiative that highlights Dakhni culture while gently and playfully addressing sexism, homophobia, and other social issues.

b: Speaker Rahul Pandita is a journalist known for his reporting from war-torn areas. Our Friends in Good Houses (2025) is his debut novel. He is also the author of Hello, Bastar: The Untold Story of India’s Maoist…
f: Speaker Rahul Pandita is a journalist known for his reporting from war-torn areas. Our Friends in Good Houses (2025) is his debut novel. He is also the author of Hello, Bastar: The Untold Story of India’s Maoist Movement (2011), Our Moon Has Blood Clots: A Memoir of a Lost Home in Kashmir (2013), The Lover Boy of Bahawalpur (2021), and the co-author of The Absent State (2010). He was awarded the International Red Cross Award for conflict reporting in 2010. He is a Yale World Fellow and also the recipient of the New India Foundation Fellowship.

b: Speaker Rajat Chauhan is a leading Sports & Exercise Medicine and Musculoskeletal Medicine specialist. He is the Founder of Back 2 Fitness Clinic, Delhi, and a Visiting Faculty at the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National…
f: Speaker Rajat Chauhan is a leading Sports & Exercise Medicine and Musculoskeletal Medicine specialist. He is the Founder of Back 2 Fitness Clinic, Delhi, and a Visiting Faculty at the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy. Trained in India and the UK, he is an authority in strength training-based rehabilitation, injury prevention, and performance enhancement, with deep expertise in Kieser Training protocols. His work spans the ICC Cricket World Cup, the World Economic Forum, and advisory roles with government and sports institutions. He is also the author of bestselling health books and the Founder and former Race Director of La Ultra – The High, one of the world’s toughest ultra-marathons.

b: Speaker Rajesh Vetcha has over 30 years of experience across infrastructure, aviation, energy, banking, and sports. A passionate advocate for active lifestyle, he has been involved in local and global sporting events,…
f: Speaker Rajesh Vetcha has over 30 years of experience across infrastructure, aviation, energy, banking, and sports. A passionate advocate for active lifestyle, he has been involved in local and global sporting events, and community fitness development. He is the Founder of Hyderabad Runners and currently serves as Race Director of the NMDC Hyderabad Marathon, which is a World Athletics Label event. Professionally he was associated with IPL, Pro Kabaddi and Wrestling League teams. In the free time he dabbles with books, theatre and is also pursuing academic research.

b: Speaker Rakhshanda Jalil is a multi-award-winning translator, writer, and literary historian. She has published over 25 books and written over 50 academic papers and essays. Her books include Love in the Time of Hate:…
f: Speaker Rakhshanda Jalil is a multi-award-winning translator, writer, and literary historian. She has published over 25 books and written over 50 academic papers and essays. Her books include Love in the Time of Hate: In the Mirror of Urdu (2024), Liking Progress, Loving Change: A Literary History of the Progressive Writers Movement in Urdu (2014), a biography of Urdu feminist writer Dr Rashid Jahan, A Rebel and Her Cause (2014), and a translation of Intizar Hussain’s The Sea Lies Ahead (2015).

b: Speaker Ranjan A Ranganathan is an architect and a passionate theatre actor/director. He has been associated with The Little Theatre Hyderabad almost since its formation in the 1990s, and also with the Dramatic Circle…
f: Speaker Ranjan A Ranganathan is an architect and a passionate theatre actor/director. He has been associated with The Little Theatre Hyderabad almost since its formation in the 1990s, and also with the Dramatic Circle of Hyderabad (DCH). He has also toured England and Scotland with a theatre group based in Harrow, and directed seven plays for the Secunderabad Club Dramatic Society.

b: Speaker Ranjani Sivakumar is a renowned classical musician known for her captivating voice and authentic style. A Grade A artiste with All India Radio, she’s sung for films like Pelli Choopulu and Mental Madilo . Her…
f: Speaker Ranjani Sivakumar is a renowned classical musician known for her captivating voice and authentic style. A Grade A artiste with All India Radio, she’s sung for films like Pelli Choopulu and Mental Madilo . Her projects, like “Raga and Yoga” and “Triobroma”, have garnered acclaim. She teaches at Jiddu Krishnamurti Schools in Bengaluru and Hyderabad, and has worked with Apple Inc, combining her tech and music skills. Her music has taken her worldwide, enriching her life experience.

b: Speaker Ravi Chellam is a wildlife biologist and conservation scientist with a PhD on Asiatic lions in Gir. He has played a key role in lion conservation, including serving as an expert advisor to the Forest Bench of…
f: Speaker Ravi Chellam is a wildlife biologist and conservation scientist with a PhD on Asiatic lions in Gir. He has played a key role in lion conservation, including serving as an expert advisor to the Forest Bench of the Supreme Court of India, which ordered the translocation of lions from Gir to Kuno. He has held leadership roles at the Wildlife Institute of India, UNDP-India, Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment, Wildlife Conservation Society–India, Greenpeace-India, among others. Currently, the CEO of Metastring Foundation, Professor at The University of Trans-Disciplinary Health Sciences and Technology, and co-ordinator of the Biodiversity Collaborative, he champions evidence-based conservation.

b: Speaker Rekha Bhatnagar is a post-graduate in Painting from Udaipur University and a former Head of the Department of Art, Kanoria College, Jaipur, Rajasthan. She is also a contemporary artist, and in a career spanning…
f: Speaker Rekha Bhatnagar is a post-graduate in Painting from Udaipur University and a former Head of the Department of Art, Kanoria College, Jaipur, Rajasthan. She is also a contemporary artist, and in a career spanning over 50 years, she has participated in many group exhibitions, workshops, and held three solo shows, including one in Guelph, Canada. Her doctoral thesis was on the folk art of the Udaipur region. She has written several articles for art and culture journals and authored two books: Dhulichitra: Folk Floor Designs of India (2019) and Gobar Dhan : Artistic Visual Expressions in Cow Dung (2025).

b: Speaker Ria Chopra ’s writing on India’s young people and internet culture has appeared in Vogue , VICE , Buzzfeed , The Hindu , The Indian Express , Refinery29 , Insider , The Quint , among others. Her portfolio career…
f: Speaker Ria Chopra ’s writing on India’s young people and internet culture has appeared in Vogue , VICE , Buzzfeed , The Hindu , The Indian Express , Refinery29 , Insider , The Quint , among others. Her portfolio career and innumerable side quests have taken her from a leadership summit at the Google HQ in Mountain View, California, to the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, to present her work, and to the hot seat of Kaun Banega Crorepati. Never Logged Out: How the Internet Created India’s Gen Z (2025) is her first book. B Kinnera Murthy Festival Director Peggy Mohan Speaker Phejin Konyak Speaker

b: Speaker Richa Sharma has a Master’s in Mass Communication from the University of Hyderabad. Finding Home Again: Our Quest to Belong (2025) is her debut novel. She has lived in different parts of the country, including…
f: Speaker Richa Sharma has a Master’s in Mass Communication from the University of Hyderabad. Finding Home Again: Our Quest to Belong (2025) is her debut novel. She has lived in different parts of the country, including in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, and has drawn on her experience of displacement. Her innumerable train journeys and first-hand experience of monsoon-led floods instigated her to write her novel. She is currently working on her next fiction and a collection of poems. Her writings have been published in the literary magazines eFiction India , Storizen , and the Hans India .

b: Rithika Fernandes drives outreach and impact at Roundglass Sustain. With a background in ecology, she is drawn to the evolving relationships between people and nature.
f: Rithika Fernandes drives outreach and impact at Roundglass Sustain. With a background in ecology, she is drawn to the evolving relationships between people and nature.

b: Speaker Ritu Sharma is a linguist and journalist with People’s Archive of Rural India (PARI). She anchors PARI’s Endangered Languages Project (ELP), which documents India’s vulnerable languages through the voices and…
f: Speaker Ritu Sharma is a linguist and journalist with People’s Archive of Rural India (PARI). She anchors PARI’s Endangered Languages Project (ELP), which documents India’s vulnerable languages through the voices and lived experiences of the people who speak them. This project is integral to the broader work of PARI, a living journal and online archive that covers rural India, capturing its diversity, including livelihoods, arts, culture, and literature. PARI documents this reality through videos, photos, audio, and articles. The archive publishes in 15 Indian languages, including English, and maintains a free online library, providing a valuable resource for communities, students, and researchers.

b: Speaker Rochelle Potkar is a prize-winning poet, author, and screenwriter. Her books include Four Degrees of Separation (2016), Paper Asylum (2018, shortlisted for the Rabindranath Tagore Literary Prize 2020), Bombay…
f: Speaker Rochelle Potkar is a prize-winning poet, author, and screenwriter. Her books include Four Degrees of Separation (2016), Paper Asylum (2018, shortlisted for the Rabindranath Tagore Literary Prize 2020), Bombay Hangovers (2021), and Coins in Rivers (2024, shortlisted for The Wise Owl Literary Award 2025). Alumna of Iowa’s International Writing Program, USA, and a Charles Wallace Fellow, University of Stirling, she has served as a creative-writing mentor at the Iowa International Writing Program and teaches poetry at the Himalayan Writing Retreat. Her writing has been translated into multiple languages, and her short film Salad (Shezari) was released in November 2025. The D’Costa Family (2025) is her debut novel.

b: Speaker Rohini Chintha experiments with methods to communicate Science both in the classroom and on various storytelling platforms. She variously plays the role of science teacher, science communicator, children’s…
f: Speaker Rohini Chintha experiments with methods to communicate Science both in the classroom and on various storytelling platforms. She variously plays the role of science teacher, science communicator, children’s writer, storyteller, Telugu translator, and You-tuber. She has received awards for her research, storytelling, writing and for her creative approach to communicating science using stories. She currently teaches Biotechnology at the Department of Genetics and Biotechnology, Veeranari Chakali Ilamma Womens’ University (formerly University college for women), Hyderabad. She founded Pop-Sci-Cles (popular Science and common tales) in 2019. Her book ‘Startlingly simple’ is her first foray into book-length popular science.

b: Speaker Rohini Subrahmanyam is a science writer at the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru. She also does freelance science journalism, mostly covering life sciences and health. She loves writing about weird…
f: Speaker Rohini Subrahmanyam is a science writer at the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru. She also does freelance science journalism, mostly covering life sciences and health. She loves writing about weird creatures on our planet, with occasional forays into climate science and physics. She has a PhD in biology from NCBS and postdoctoral experience in developmental biology from Harvard University. After her postdoc, she transitioned into science writing, with bylines in Scientific American , New Scientist, Science News, Knowable, Nautilus , LiveScience , The Scientist , The Hindu , and others.

b: Speaker Rohit Chakravarty is a bat researcher working with Nature Conservation Foundation and Bat Conservation International. Over the past decade, he has studied the bats of the Andaman Islands and Uttarakhand, and…
f: Speaker Rohit Chakravarty is a bat researcher working with Nature Conservation Foundation and Bat Conservation International. Over the past decade, he has studied the bats of the Andaman Islands and Uttarakhand, and currently leads projects related to bat conservation in India. He is passionate about public speaking and campaigning for bats.

b: Speaker Rohit Chawla is a leading contemporary photographer. His solo exhibitions include ‘Wanderlust’, ‘Tribute to Raja Ravi Varma’, ‘Klimt — The Sequel’, ‘Free da! — The Homage’, ‘World of Wearable Art’, ‘Goa Style &…
f: Speaker Rohit Chawla is a leading contemporary photographer. His solo exhibitions include ‘Wanderlust’, ‘Tribute to Raja Ravi Varma’, ‘Klimt — The Sequel’, ‘Free da! — The Homage’, ‘World of Wearable Art’, ‘Goa Style & The Inspired Frame’, ‘Artist — Unboxed’, ‘The Quiet Portrait’, ‘Untangling the Politics of Hair’, ‘Banned Books’, and the ‘Havana’ exhibition in 2024. He conceptualized and photographed over 400 magazine covers. His recent photographic work won India its first-ever Industry Craft Gold Lion at Cannes (2023), the Grand Prix at Spikes Asia (2024), and the Grand Prix at the Abbies (2024). The Indian Accent Cookbook (2016), The Fine Art of Food , and The Bangla Table from Chettinad (2014) are his food books.

b: Speaker Ruchir Joshi is the author of The Last Jet-Engine Laugh (2000), a novel, and Poriborton! (2011), a book about the 2011 state elections in West Bengal. His latest book, The Great Eastern Hotel (2025), is a work…
f: Speaker Ruchir Joshi is the author of The Last Jet-Engine Laugh (2000), a novel, and Poriborton! (2011), a book about the 2011 state elections in West Bengal. His latest book, The Great Eastern Hotel (2025), is a work of historical fiction set in Calcutta during World War II. He has been a columnist for The Telegraph , The Hindu , The Economic Times , and other newspapers, and has contributed to Granta , India Magazine , Man’s World , Seminar , E-Flux , Wittede Witt Review , and The Indian Quarterly . He has also directed documentaries and essay films, including the award-winning Tales from Planet Kolkata (1993).

b: Speaker Rueben Dass is a Malaysian author of two novels: The Number Four (2021) and Ski (2025). His short stories, poetry, and screenplays have appeared on literary platforms such as Anak Sastra and Men Matters Online…
f: Speaker Rueben Dass is a Malaysian author of two novels: The Number Four (2021) and Ski (2025). His short stories, poetry, and screenplays have appeared on literary platforms such as Anak Sastra and Men Matters Online Journal . His screenplay Mayat was among the Top 10 finalists out of 144 entries in the 3rd Kuman Pictures Screenwriting Contest, organised by Malaysian production house Kuman Pictures. He has also authored more than 60 articles on international security, foreign affairs, and political violence, published in various international media outlets. He has lived in Kuala Lumpur and London and currently works at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore.

b: Speaker Rushikesh Chavan is the Director of The Habitats Trust, bringing over 25 years of experience in driving impactful solutions to some of the world’s most complex challenges arising from biodiversity loss and…
f: Speaker Rushikesh Chavan is the Director of The Habitats Trust, bringing over 25 years of experience in driving impactful solutions to some of the world’s most complex challenges arising from biodiversity loss and climate change. His expertise spans strategy development, organisational stewardship, biodiversity, regenerative development, and fostering collaborative partnerships. He integrates conservation biology, ecology, economics, psychology, and data analytics to provide actionable policy insights that drive change. Dinesh C.

b: Speaker Sadhna Chaganti is a climate and sustainability professional with a deep interest in integrating art, culture, and climate resilience. Through her work, she explores how traditional Indian art forms can act as…
f: Speaker Sadhna Chaganti is a climate and sustainability professional with a deep interest in integrating art, culture, and climate resilience. Through her work, she explores how traditional Indian art forms can act as powerful tools for environmental storytelling, community engagement, and healing. She has been involved in curating and facilitating art-based workshops that revive indigenous art practices while linking them to contemporary themes of sustainability and climate adaptation.

b: Speaker Sahana Ghosh is an award-winning journalist with an eye on science and the environment. She currently serves as the Associate Editor at Nature India , where she contributes to editorial strategy and function.…
f: Speaker Sahana Ghosh is an award-winning journalist with an eye on science and the environment. She currently serves as the Associate Editor at Nature India , where she contributes to editorial strategy and function. She was the 2023 Journalist in Residence at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science in Berlin, examining the history of ocean science across the Indian Ocean. She is a co-founder and secretary of the Science Journalists Association of India, a member of the inaugural Oxford Climate Journalism Network, and in 2021, was named one of 16 Women Restoring the Earth by the Global Landscapes Forum.

b: Speaker Sally Varma is a senior specialist in the Farm Animal Protection department at Humane World for Animals India. With over two decades of experience in animal welfare, she has worked across companion animal…
f: Speaker Sally Varma is a senior specialist in the Farm Animal Protection department at Humane World for Animals India. With over two decades of experience in animal welfare, she has worked across companion animal protection, farm animal welfare, and disaster management for animals. She received the 100 Women Achievers Award conferred by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, from the President of India in 2016, and many other recognitions for her work in Kerala. She is a Tedx speaker and is deeply engaged in outreach and engagement, making complex issues around animal protection relatable and accessible to the public.

b: Speaker Salma , a poet, novelist, and activist who goes by the pen name of Rajathi, is a significant voice in contemporary Tamil literature. Her renowned novel Irandam Jaamangalin Kathai (2004, The Long Hours of the…
f: Speaker Salma , a poet, novelist, and activist who goes by the pen name of Rajathi, is a significant voice in contemporary Tamil literature. Her renowned novel Irandam Jaamangalin Kathai (2004, The Long Hours of the Night ) was longlisted for the Man Asia Prize in 2009. Her writing challenges deeply entrenched social and patriarchal norms, particularly within the Tamil Muslim community of her origin. Her poetry collections, Oru Maalaiyum Innoru Maalaiyum (2000) and Pachchai Devathai (2003), are celebrated for their incisive exploration of female experience. Her poetry and fiction have been translated into multiple languages. She was recently nominated to the Rajya Sabha.

b: Speaker Samanth Subramanian is an award-winning writer and journalist whose work has appeared in the New Yorker , The New York Times , WIRED , Granta , Harper’s , the Wall Street Journal , and is a contributing writer…
f: Speaker Samanth Subramanian is an award-winning writer and journalist whose work has appeared in the New Yorker , The New York Times , WIRED , Granta , Harper’s , the Wall Street Journal , and is a contributing writer for the Guardian Long Read . He is also the author of three books: Following Fish: Travels Around the Indian Coast (2010), This Divided Island: Stories from the Sri Lankan War (2014), and A Dominant Character: The Radical Science and Restless Politics of J. B. S. Haldane (2019).

b: Speaker Sameer Hamdani is an architect, conservationist, and art historian. His conservation works in Kashmir include the conservation of Mughal gardens, Aali Masjid and Khanqah-i Maula, and the reconstruction of Pir…
f: Speaker Sameer Hamdani is an architect, conservationist, and art historian. His conservation works in Kashmir include the conservation of Mughal gardens, Aali Masjid and Khanqah-i Maula, and the reconstruction of Pir Dastgir Saheb Shrine. In 2021, he oversaw the successful nomination of Srinagar on UNESCO’s Creative Cities Network. He has also written widely on South Asian material culture. He is a 2023-24 recipient of a conservation grant from The Barakat Trust (London) for a documentation project of architectural epigraphy in early modern Kashmir. In 2021-22, he was the Aga Khan Fellow in Islamic Architecture, Conservation & Urbanism at MIT, Cambridge.

b: Speaker Sameer Rahat (SR) is a Bombay-based composer, lyricist and performer whose work sits at the intersection of film, poetry and performing arts. A unique blend of poetic recitation and universal musicality that has…
f: Speaker Sameer Rahat (SR) is a Bombay-based composer, lyricist and performer whose work sits at the intersection of film, poetry and performing arts. A unique blend of poetic recitation and universal musicality that has its roots in self-styled Urdu Blues and UEM (Urdu Electronica Music), his art is not merely an auditory experience, it is cinema for the ears. A regular at India’s most prestigious festivals and cultural venues, SR has also brought his voice to international stages with tours across Europe, including Germany and the UK.

b: Speaker Sameer Shisodia has headed the Rainmatter Foundation since its founding in late 2020. His concern for food systems, climate, and the biodiversity collapse has led him away from his earlier tech avatar. He runs a…
f: Speaker Sameer Shisodia has headed the Rainmatter Foundation since its founding in late 2020. His concern for food systems, climate, and the biodiversity collapse has led him away from his earlier tech avatar. He runs a small, locally focused travel outfit, created regenerative farming collectives, and at the Rainmatter Foundation, is trying to figure out ways to create mainstream change to address this most critical issue the species has ever faced.

b: Speaker Sanjaya Baru is the author of Secession of the Successful: The Flight Out of New India (2025), India’s Power Elite: Class, Caste and A Cultural Revolution (2021), 1991: How P.V. Narasimha Rao Made History…
f: Speaker Sanjaya Baru is the author of Secession of the Successful: The Flight Out of New India (2025), India’s Power Elite: Class, Caste and A Cultural Revolution (2021), 1991: How P.V. Narasimha Rao Made History (2016), The Accidental Prime Minister: The Making and Unmaking of Manmohan Singh (2014), and Journey of a Nation: 75 Years of the Indian Economy (2022) . He served as editor of the Economic Times , the Financial Express , and Business Standard , editorial-page editor of the Times of India , and the Indian Express . He was media adviser to former prime minister Manmohan Singh and director for geo-economics and strategy, International Institute of Strategic Studies, London. He taught at universities in India and abroad.

b: Speaker Sarah Hyder Iqbal is an independent researcher, practitioner, and trainer who champions creative and participatory approaches to connect science with society. She co-founded Superheroes Against Superbugs to…
f: Speaker Sarah Hyder Iqbal is an independent researcher, practitioner, and trainer who champions creative and participatory approaches to connect science with society. She co-founded Superheroes Against Superbugs to tackle Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) and has developed and contributed to innovative projects like Planet DIVOC-91, The Explorer Series, Arting Health for Impact, and the India Science Festival. Her research focuses on science communication and promoting fair, meaningful knowledge exchange between researchers and communities. With a PhD in Biochemistry from the University of Oxford and postdoctoral research at The Scripps Research Institute, USA, she has led innovative programmes blending science, policy, arts, and community action.

b: Speaker Sarah Zia is the Senior Commissioning Editor at Penguin Select, Penguin Random House India. Since beginning her publishing journey in 2019, she’s been drawn to stories that linger—ones that bridge distances and…
f: Speaker Sarah Zia is the Senior Commissioning Editor at Penguin Select, Penguin Random House India. Since beginning her publishing journey in 2019, she’s been drawn to stories that linger—ones that bridge distances and remind us of our shared humanity. A UCLA graduate in English Literature and Communication Studies, she finds resonance in the quiet brilliance of Samuel Beckett and George Eliot. M.L. Stedman’s The Light Between (2012) remains a story that has stayed with her through the years. At HLF, she represents Letters from Gaza (2025) by Mohammed Al-Zaqzooq and Mahmoud Alshaer.

b: Speaker Sathya Raghu is the CEO of Soul Forest, building India’s first Nature Economic Zones that blend ecological restoration with long-term economic wellbeing. He is the author of Soul Forest and the Children Who…
f: Speaker Sathya Raghu is the CEO of Soul Forest, building India’s first Nature Economic Zones that blend ecological restoration with long-term economic wellbeing. He is the author of Soul Forest and the Children Who Heard the Earth’s Secrets (2025), and an Earthshot Prize-winning social entrepreneur. Soul Forest’s decade-long goal is to restore 100,000 acres of barren land into biodiverse forests. The question that guides his work now is how to help a billion humans remember that nature is our ancestor and to move a billion dollars toward restoring it.

b: Speaker Sayan Basu is the Prof. D. Balasubramanian Chair of Eye Research and serves as the Director of both the Prof. Brien Holden Eye Research Centre (BHERC) and the Centre for Ocular Regeneration (CORE) at the L V…
f: Speaker Sayan Basu is the Prof. D. Balasubramanian Chair of Eye Research and serves as the Director of both the Prof. Brien Holden Eye Research Centre (BHERC) and the Centre for Ocular Regeneration (CORE) at the L V Prasad Eye Institute. Clinician-scientist and a key opinion leader in corneal and ocular surface disorders, he has significantly contributed to advancements in regenerative medicine and translational research. His research focuses on scarless corneal wound healing through innovations in stem cells, biomaterials, and 3D bioprinting. His ability to tackle intricate medical and scientific challenges with innovative solutions is widely regarded. He has published over 260 peer-reviewed articles in international scientific journals.

b: Speaker Serish Nanisetti is a journalist and writer, known for his reporting on politics, economy, culture, and urban life. Deeply interested in history, museums, and the lived textures of cities, he writes with an eye…
f: Speaker Serish Nanisetti is a journalist and writer, known for his reporting on politics, economy, culture, and urban life. Deeply interested in history, museums, and the lived textures of cities, he writes with an eye for context and consequence. He brings a journalist’s curiosity and a storyteller’s instinct to conversations on Hyderabad’s history.

b: Speaker Sesha Sindhu Rao started her career as an assistant director over a decade ago and is now a director, writer, and producer. She explores diverse genres and pushes the boundaries in her pursuit to tell compelling…
f: Speaker Sesha Sindhu Rao started her career as an assistant director over a decade ago and is now a director, writer, and producer. She explores diverse genres and pushes the boundaries in her pursuit to tell compelling stories and make impactful films. She is the writer-director of Choosi Choodangaane (2020), producer of the National Award-winning Gandhi Tatha Chettu (2025), the writer-director of the forthcoming web series Kanyasulkam , and the writer of an untitled miniseries.

b: Speaker Shashi Kumar is Co-Founder & CEO of Akshayakalpa Organic. He did his bachelor’s in computer science, worked at Wipro Technologies, and completed his master’s in telecommunication engineering at the Illinois…
f: Speaker Shashi Kumar is Co-Founder & CEO of Akshayakalpa Organic. He did his bachelor’s in computer science, worked at Wipro Technologies, and completed his master’s in telecommunication engineering at the Illinois Institute of Technology, Chicago. After 17 years in the technology industry, he returned home to rethink and recreate the country’s farm sector to improve the economic conditions of small and marginal farmers. With the veterinarian and entrepreneur Dr GNS Reddy and the support of colleagues, he started Akshayakalpa in 2010, which has grown to become India’s largest certified organic milk company. A majority of the 850 farmers who are part of the Akshayakalpa movement have improved their earnings by 3-4 times.

b: Speaker Shashidhar Nanjundaiah ’s writing is informed by his extensive academic and media practice. His recent book News Aesthetics and Myth: The Making of Media Illiteracy in India (2024) uses two studies of…
f: Speaker Shashidhar Nanjundaiah ’s writing is informed by his extensive academic and media practice. His recent book News Aesthetics and Myth: The Making of Media Illiteracy in India (2024) uses two studies of hypervisibilization and invisibilization from Hathras and Ahmedabad to evaluate how the enduring practices of “presentation” and “absentation” inform our world, resulting in an absurd situation of illiteracy in a media-saturated world. He is an educationist focused on bridging industry-academic gaps in private institutes of media and communication. He holds a PhD from Southern Illinois University, Carbondale, and currently serves as the founding Dean and Professor of the School of Digital Media and Communication at Mahindra University in Hyderabad.

b: Speaker Shatabdi Chakrabarti is a visual storyteller. Her work focuses on wildlife, conservation, and indigenous communities. She has been documenting on-ground environmental issues and traditional practices for over 15…
f: Speaker Shatabdi Chakrabarti is a visual storyteller. Her work focuses on wildlife, conservation, and indigenous communities. She has been documenting on-ground environmental issues and traditional practices for over 15 years. Her work and personal projects have taken her to remote areas of India, where she has spent time in the wilderness with the local communities documenting their stories and experiencing the reality of co-existence. She is an award-winning and internationally exhibited, and published photographer, researcher, and filmmaker.

b: Speaker Shawn Sebastian is a documentary film maker and an independent journalist. He is the founder of ‘Storyental Media’, a production house specialising in development-centred multimedia content. He contributes to…
f: Speaker Shawn Sebastian is a documentary film maker and an independent journalist. He is the founder of ‘Storyental Media’, a production house specialising in development-centred multimedia content. He contributes to national and international media outlets on subjects such as climate change, culture, education, food security, human rights, women empowerment, and ordinary people who make a difference. He has directed and shot documentaries, short films for state governments, nonprofit organisations, and for news platforms such as Associated Press, Aljazeera, BBC and Discovery. He has won two UN awards for his development oriented short films.

b: Speaker Shikha Jain has been associated with social organizations working on diverse issues, including mental health, education, and animal protection. She has been working towards animal welfare since her college…
f: Speaker Shikha Jain has been associated with social organizations working on diverse issues, including mental health, education, and animal protection. She has been working towards animal welfare since her college years, and found her calling in the plant-based movement 14 years ago when she learnt about its immense power to resolve many issues faced by our planet. At Humane World for Animals India, she works as Manager for the Public Outreach campaign through which she reaches out to various institutions to make them aware of animal welfare and facilitate their plant-based consumption.

b: Speaker Shobha Tharoor Srinivasan is an award-winning author of a dozen books and a celebrated voice-over artist who received the Best Narration Award at India’s 68th National Film Awards (2022). Indi-Alphabet (2018),…
f: Speaker Shobha Tharoor Srinivasan is an award-winning author of a dozen books and a celebrated voice-over artist who received the Best Narration Award at India’s 68th National Film Awards (2022). Indi-Alphabet (2018), winner of the Purple Dragonfly Award for Cultural Diversity, and It’s Time to Rhyme (2022), Publishing Next’s Best Children’s Book of the Year 2022, and Prince with a Paintbrush: The Story of Raja Ravi Varma , named a 2022 Best Book of the Year by Beyond the Box Kids are among her most celebrated titles. Her Let’s Use Our Words (2025) is an innovative book that blends prose, poetry, and games to make language joyful and interactive.

b: Speaker Shubha Ranganathan is an associate professor in the Department of Liberal Arts at, Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad. She draws on qualitative approaches and interdisciplinary perspectives in research…
f: Speaker Shubha Ranganathan is an associate professor in the Department of Liberal Arts at, Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad. She draws on qualitative approaches and interdisciplinary perspectives in research projects in (mental) health, gender, and disability. She studied local healing practices among marginalised groups and mental health and disability-related issues in India. Grounded in critical and social justice perspectives, her work focuses on lived experiences and the role of advocacy for social change. She is exploring questions about parenting and care in the context of autism as part of her engagement with the neurodiversity discourse.

b: Speaker Sibghat Khan is an architect, researcher, and curator whose work explores Deccani Islamicate history, urban memory, and architectural heritage. Founder of The DeccanArchive , he specializes in documenting…
f: Speaker Sibghat Khan is an architect, researcher, and curator whose work explores Deccani Islamicate history, urban memory, and architectural heritage. Founder of The DeccanArchive , he specializes in documenting historic environments through drawing, narrative, and fieldwork. His projects span exhibitions, conservation-focused research, and public scholarship, including major studies on the Musi River and Qutb Shahi architecture. His practice brings together archival inquiry and contemporary storytelling to make the Deccan ’s layered past accessible to wider audiences.

b: Speaker Siddarth Koul completed his degree in Mass Media in 2021 and entered the film industry as an Assistant Director in 2022, learning under renowned filmmakers like Nikkhil Advani, Abhay Pannu, Raaj Shaandilyaa, and…
f: Speaker Siddarth Koul completed his degree in Mass Media in 2021 and entered the film industry as an Assistant Director in 2022, learning under renowned filmmakers like Nikkhil Advani, Abhay Pannu, Raaj Shaandilyaa, and Ashima Chibber. His work includes projects such as Mumbai Diaries Season 2 , Rocket Boys Season 2 , and Mrs. Chatterjee vs. Norway , and VVKWWV . Along with Ankit Wali, he combines their experience in fiction, documentary, theatre, and mainstream entertainment to tell rooted, emotional stories that resonate across borders.

b: Speaker Siddhartha Gigoo won the 2015 Commonwealth Short Story Prize for “The Umbrella Man.” His publications include A Fistful of Earth and Other Stories (2015); two co-edited anthologies, A Long Dream of Home: The…
f: Speaker Siddhartha Gigoo won the 2015 Commonwealth Short Story Prize for “The Umbrella Man.” His publications include A Fistful of Earth and Other Stories (2015); two co-edited anthologies, A Long Dream of Home: The Persecution , Exodus and Exile of Kashmiri Pandits (2015), Once We Had Everything: Literature in Exile (2019); two poetry books, Fall and Other Poems (1994), Reflections (1995) ; four novels, The Garden of Solitude (2011) , Mehr: A Love Story (2018) , The Lion of Kashmir (2020), Love in the Time of Quarantine (2020); and a memoir, A Long Season of Ashes (2024). His short films, The Last Day (2013) and Goodbye, Mayfly (2015), have won several awards.

b: Speaker Sita Reddy is a writer, scholar and curator. She has been visiting professor at University of Hyderabad, and fellow at the Smithsonian and Sangam House. Her recent nonfiction writing is on the fate of botanical…
f: Speaker Sita Reddy is a writer, scholar and curator. She has been visiting professor at University of Hyderabad, and fellow at the Smithsonian and Sangam House. Her recent nonfiction writing is on the fate of botanical art in global archives through her favourite literary form: the essay. In 2026 her MARG volume, Weight of a Petal: Ars Botanica (launched at HLF in 2019) will be republished as a revised book edition.

b: Sneha Banerjee teaches political science at the University of Hyderabad. She researches and writes on the politics of reproduction and questions of gender in law and policy. An alumna of JNU, Delhi, she pursued…
f: Sneha Banerjee teaches political science at the University of Hyderabad. She researches and writes on the politics of reproduction and questions of gender in law and policy. An alumna of JNU, Delhi, she pursued postdoctoral research at the University of Zürich. She is also an associate at the Global Institute of Emerging Human Mobilities, University of Technology, Sydney.

b: Speaker Sneha Kanakala is a Mass Communication student and a passionate theatre practitioner. With training from the Lee Strasberg Theatre and Film Institute, New York, and Adishakti, she experiments with voice,…
f: Speaker Sneha Kanakala is a Mass Communication student and a passionate theatre practitioner. With training from the Lee Strasberg Theatre and Film Institute, New York, and Adishakti, she experiments with voice, movement, and presence to tell stories that linger.

b: Speaker Somdatta Karak is a biologist turned science communicator. She makes biology more accessible and understandable to young people. She co-founded SciCity, Hyderabad, to bring science to cultural conversations of…
f: Speaker Somdatta Karak is a biologist turned science communicator. She makes biology more accessible and understandable to young people. She co-founded SciCity, Hyderabad, to bring science to cultural conversations of the city. She heads science communication and public outreach at CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB).

b: Speaker Sonali Rasal is an award-winning poet who writes in English, Hindustani, and Marathi. Founder of poetry communities in Pune, she conducts art-writing workshops and has recited at prestigious literary festivals,…
f: Speaker Sonali Rasal is an award-winning poet who writes in English, Hindustani, and Marathi. Founder of poetry communities in Pune, she conducts art-writing workshops and has recited at prestigious literary festivals, including the Tata International Litfest, Mumbai Litfest, PILF, Jashn-e-Adab, Unerase-Poetrystaan, and India Soulfest. Working with an NGO bringing art and poetry to slums in Pune, she mentors children to recite on bigger platforms, including TedX. Her book of poems, # The ‘L’ Word (2021), has been received well at various Book Fairs.

b: Speaker Sonam Samat is an entrepreneur and educator. After graduating from BITS Pilani, she did her PhD in Behavioural Sciences in the US. She moved back to Hyderabad in 2024 and started Flavour Lab, where she teaches…
f: Speaker Sonam Samat is an entrepreneur and educator. After graduating from BITS Pilani, she did her PhD in Behavioural Sciences in the US. She moved back to Hyderabad in 2024 and started Flavour Lab, where she teaches children how to cook delicious, nutritious, and sustainable foods through games, activities, and hands-on cooking classes. Flavour Lab has built India’s first Food Education curriculum and is partnering with schools in Hyderabad and Bangalore to introduce Food as a subject for children.

b: Speaker Sowmya Dechamma teaches at the Centre for Comparative Literature, University of Hyderabad. She researches in the areas of Cultural Discourses in Contemporary India, Translation Studies, Literatures of India,…
f: Speaker Sowmya Dechamma teaches at the Centre for Comparative Literature, University of Hyderabad. She researches in the areas of Cultural Discourses in Contemporary India, Translation Studies, Literatures of India, Minority Language and Politics, and Kodava performative cultures. Her articles have appeared in international journals and national newspapers. She taught at the City University of New York as part of her Fulbright during 2019–20 and was a Commonwealth Fellow at the University of Southampton during 2010-11. She has published a co-edited book, Cinemas of South India (2010), and a monograph/book, Languages of Minority: Orality, Translation and Desiring English (2024).

b: Speaker Sridala Swami is the author of three collections of poetry, including Run for the Shadows (2021, reprinted 2022). She has served on the Jury of the Montreal International Poetry Prize (2019) and the Rayaprol…
f: Speaker Sridala Swami is the author of three collections of poetry, including Run for the Shadows (2021, reprinted 2022). She has served on the Jury of the Montreal International Poetry Prize (2019) and the Rayaprol Poetry Prize (2023).

b: Speaker Srikar Raghavan is an independent writer and researcher. His first degree was in engineering, before he decided to switch to the humanities, where he has remained. He is a recipient of a New India Foundation…
f: Speaker Srikar Raghavan is an independent writer and researcher. His first degree was in engineering, before he decided to switch to the humanities, where he has remained. He is a recipient of a New India Foundation fellowship. His debut book, Rama Bhima Soma: Cultural Investigations into Modern Karnataka (2025), won the award for Best Non-Fiction at the Atta Galatta Prize in 2025.

b: Speaker Srilekha Kaluvakunta is the author of Unique Thinking: Thought Management for Uniqueness in Thinking and Unique Thought Process (2019), a book based on a pioneering concept. She works as a Management Executive…
f: Speaker Srilekha Kaluvakunta is the author of Unique Thinking: Thought Management for Uniqueness in Thinking and Unique Thought Process (2019), a book based on a pioneering concept. She works as a Management Executive at Infosys, and also as Vice President for Education and Social Impact for G20 Global Excellence, Independent Board Director for a Cybersecurity firm, and Director for Social Wellbeing at NGOs focused on social uplift and positive social transformation of people and society. She is recognized as an Indian Glory, Indian Icon, and received the Emerging Leader of the Year Award from India’s G20 Forum, and the Outstanding Indian Achievers Award from the Indian Achievers Forum.

b: Speaker ​​Sriramoju Haragopal ’s curiosity about the name of his village in the Yadadri-Bhongir district led him into deeper historical research. ‘Kotta Telangana Charitra Brundam’ (New Telangana History Group), a…
f: Speaker ​​Sriramoju Haragopal ’s curiosity about the name of his village in the Yadadri-Bhongir district led him into deeper historical research. ‘Kotta Telangana Charitra Brundam’ (New Telangana History Group), a coming together of students and colleagues, took up important work when he worked with the history wing of Telangana Jagruti from 2013 to 2019. The nearly 150-strong group travels and brings out ever-new findings almost every week, and has succeeded in enlarging and deepening the historical and cultural knowledge and scholarship about Telangana.

b: Srirupa Chatterjee teaches in the Department of Liberal Arts at IIT Hyderabad. Her publications include Global Literatures and Cultures of Modernity: Critical Perspectives from India (2025), Female Body Image in…
f: Srirupa Chatterjee teaches in the Department of Liberal Arts at IIT Hyderabad. Her publications include Global Literatures and Cultures of Modernity: Critical Perspectives from India (2025), Female Body Image in Contemporary Indian Literature and Culture (2024), Gendered Violence in Public Spaces: Women’s Narratives of Travel in Neoliberal India (2023), and research papers in international journals.

b: Speaker Stanly Johny is the International Affairs Editor with The Hindu . A PhD in international studies from the Centre for West Asian Studies, JNU, New Delhi, he anchors the paper’s international coverage, besides…
f: Speaker Stanly Johny is the International Affairs Editor with The Hindu . A PhD in international studies from the Centre for West Asian Studies, JNU, New Delhi, he anchors the paper’s international coverage, besides writing editorials, Op-Eds, and other reportage. He has also contributed to think tanks in India and abroad. His work includes The ISIS Caliphate: From Syria to the Doorsteps of India (2018), the co-authored The Comrades and the Mullahs: China, Afghanistan and the New Asian Geopolitics (2022), and Original Sin: Israel, Palestine and the Revenge of Old West Asia (2024). He is a Visiting Professor at KREA University and an adjunct faculty at Asian College of Journalism.

b: Speaker Subhatul Marjan is an English language trainer and consultant, and a poet at heart, writing mainly in Urdu. Her poetry explores themes of feminism, self-realization, and defiance, echoing her heart’s deepest…
f: Speaker Subhatul Marjan is an English language trainer and consultant, and a poet at heart, writing mainly in Urdu. Her poetry explores themes of feminism, self-realization, and defiance, echoing her heart’s deepest emotions. She sees writing as a form of catharsis, therapy, and connection with others.

b: Speaker Suchitra Shenoy is a writer and teacher in the Buddhist tradition. Her previous book, Mindful Parenting (2016), was on Amazon India’s Top Parenting Books list. Her first book (co-authored with Pavithra Mehta),…
f: Speaker Suchitra Shenoy is a writer and teacher in the Buddhist tradition. Her previous book, Mindful Parenting (2016), was on Amazon India’s Top Parenting Books list. Her first book (co-authored with Pavithra Mehta), Infinite Vision (2011), was on Amazon’s Top 40 Management Books and a finalist for the US Academy of Management’s George Terry Award. It has been translated into Japanese, Portuguese, and Tamil. She teaches from the discourses of the Buddha, emphasising practice in daily life. She holds degrees from Brandeis University and the London School of Economics. Dinesh C.

b: Speaker Sujeeth Anne is a self-taught naturalist and conservationist. He is an independent researcher and founder of Meraki, an organisation that has rescued more than 8000 turtles, tortoises, and other animals,…
f: Speaker Sujeeth Anne is a self-taught naturalist and conservationist. He is an independent researcher and founder of Meraki, an organisation that has rescued more than 8000 turtles, tortoises, and other animals, rehabilitated and released them back into the wild.

b: Speaker Sumana Kasturi is a writer and educator specialising in feminist media studies and childhood studies. Her research explores how children make meaning through play and reading, storytelling, and digital practice.…
f: Speaker Sumana Kasturi is a writer and educator specialising in feminist media studies and childhood studies. Her research explores how children make meaning through play and reading, storytelling, and digital practice. She is the co-editor of the anthology Childscape, Mediascape: Children and Media in India (2023) and the author of the book Gender, Citizenship and Identity in the Indian Blogosphere (2020). Her work has appeared in the Wire , India Forum , and other academic and popular publications.

b: Speaker Sumanaspati Reddy served All India Radio as producer-broadcaster for over three decades, and dabbles in his multiple interests: photography, documentary cinema, writing in English and Telugu, and organic…
f: Speaker Sumanaspati Reddy served All India Radio as producer-broadcaster for over three decades, and dabbles in his multiple interests: photography, documentary cinema, writing in English and Telugu, and organic farming. During the last decade and more, he has spent much of his professional and personal life in Adilabad, documenting and showcasing in various formats, the Adivasi and folk cultures of north Telangana from Adilabad to Mancheriyal.

b: Speaker Suneetha A is an independent researcher who works on gender, minority, violence, and law. Her recent book, Faith in Democracy: Muslim Political Political Discourse in the Telugu Region (2025) , is co-authored…
f: Speaker Suneetha A is an independent researcher who works on gender, minority, violence, and law. Her recent book, Faith in Democracy: Muslim Political Political Discourse in the Telugu Region (2025) , is co-authored with M.A.Moid. She is an avid translator of theory from English to Telugu and short stories from Telugu to English. She translated bell hooks’ Feminism is for Everybody as Andarikee Streevaadam (2025). She works with ‘Maidaanam’, a blog that discusses the culture, history, and politics of the Deccan.

b: Speaker Tanay pursued a bachelor’s in architecture, and after a brief career, he ventured into communication design at IDC, IIT Bombay, where he graduated with a gold medal. He established one of India’s largest design…
f: Speaker Tanay pursued a bachelor’s in architecture, and after a brief career, he ventured into communication design at IDC, IIT Bombay, where he graduated with a gold medal. He established one of India’s largest design studios with over 120 designers, and in 2016, his firm was acquired by Dentsu International, a Japanese advertising powerhouse. Despite his entrepreneurial success, he felt constrained by corporate structures and returned to his artistic roots. While architecture intrigued him with its historical depth, capturing moments on canvas gave him joy. Watercolour became his preferred medium, and as an established watercolourist, he has exhibited his works both in India and abroad.

b: Speaker Tanuja Chandra directed television shows, Mirch Masala and Zameen Aasmaan , co-wrote the screenplay and dialogue for Mahesh Bhatt’s films, Zakhm and Tamanna , both National award-winners, and co-wrote Yash…
f: Speaker Tanuja Chandra directed television shows, Mirch Masala and Zameen Aasmaan , co-wrote the screenplay and dialogue for Mahesh Bhatt’s films, Zakhm and Tamanna , both National award-winners, and co-wrote Yash Chopra’s Dil Toh Pagal Hai . Beginning independent film direction in 1998, she directed Dushman , Sangharsh , Sur , Hope and A Little Sugar , Qarib Qarib Singlle , two short films: Silvat and A Monsoon Date , and the feature documentary Aunty Sudha Aunty Radha . Her documentary series on matrimonial fraud Wedding.con was nominated for many awards including the Asia Content Awards at The Busan International Film Festival, and won several awards in 2024. She also published a collection of short stories Bijnis Woman (2017).

b: Speaker Tanya Sujan is a Research Associate at Kashmir Loom, where her work focuses on the study, documentation, and preservation of Kashmir’s textile heritage. Her research explores how motifs and techniques reflect…
f: Speaker Tanya Sujan is a Research Associate at Kashmir Loom, where her work focuses on the study, documentation, and preservation of Kashmir’s textile heritage. Her research explores how motifs and techniques reflect evolving cultural aesthetics over time. She contributes to the documentation of traditional weaving knowledge and the archiving of rare patterns through structured research and analysis. At the core of her practice is an admiration for Kashmir’s long-standing artistic traditions. Through her work, she presents textiles not only as objects of beauty but as living records of culture and memory.

b: Festival Director Tejah Balantrapu is Associate Director for Science, Health Data, and Storytelling at the L V Prasad Eye Institute in Hyderabad. He has a Master’s in Communications from the University of Hyderabad and…
f: Festival Director Tejah Balantrapu is Associate Director for Science, Health Data, and Storytelling at the L V Prasad Eye Institute in Hyderabad. He has a Master’s in Communications from the University of Hyderabad and has worked to promote awareness of vision loss in global policy networks for two decades. He is also an active member of the Nature Lovers of Hyderabad, an informal group of tree enthusiasts in the city. Amita R Desai Festival Director B Kinnera Murthy Festival Director Usha Raman Festival Director

b: Speaker Tejaswini Yarlagadda is a historian and heritage enthusiast. She leads Pleach India Foundation, which works to preserve and promote India’s cultural heritage through research, education, and public engagement.…
f: Speaker Tejaswini Yarlagadda is a historian and heritage enthusiast. She leads Pleach India Foundation, which works to preserve and promote India’s cultural heritage through research, education, and public engagement. Her leadership focuses on bridging academic scholarship with community participation to make history accessible and relevant. A UGC Fellow and Gold Medalist from the University of Hyderabad, she holds a PhD in History and is the author of Social History of the Deccan (2004). She was Chairperson of Indian Women Network, and currently serves as Convenor of the Culture and Tourism Panel at CII, Telangana.

b: Speaker Triparna Banerjee is a filmmaker and screenwriter. Her work has been showcased at film festivals in Toronto, Busan, CPH: DOX, Palm Springs, and Rotterdam, and acknowledged at L’atelier Cinéfondation at the…
f: Speaker Triparna Banerjee is a filmmaker and screenwriter. Her work has been showcased at film festivals in Toronto, Busan, CPH: DOX, Palm Springs, and Rotterdam, and acknowledged at L’atelier Cinéfondation at the Cannes Film Festival, HAF at the Hong Kong Film Festival, and APM at Busan International Film Festival. Her short film Nails premiered at the Red Sea International Film Festival (2024). Her documentary feature, From the Shadows , was awarded the Hatched grant by Chicken & Egg Pictures, USA, and was nominated for the One World Media Awards (2023), and received the National Awards (2024). She is a visiting faculty at Annapurna College of Film and Media and at Breda University, Netherlands.

b: Speaker Uma Damodar Sridhar has been associated with Hyderabad Literary Festival since 2012. She is currently Head, Department of French and Francophone Studies at the EFL University, Hyderabad, and teaches French…
f: Speaker Uma Damodar Sridhar has been associated with Hyderabad Literary Festival since 2012. She is currently Head, Department of French and Francophone Studies at the EFL University, Hyderabad, and teaches French language, linguistics, teaching methodology, and translation. She previously worked at the Alliance Française of Hyderabad as a teacher and translator from 1988 to 2000, and as Deputy-Director from 2005 to 2009. Her translations include two volumes of poetry Butterfly Caresses (2015) and Flying Embers (2026), and a travel narrative by Pierre Sonnerat, the 18th-century French naturalist and explorer (forthcoming).

b: Speaker Unnati Ved is the co-founder of The Lit People, a thriving book club in Hyderabad. She is an ELT professional and the founder of Eager Readers, an enrichment academy for learners of 5 to 16 years, which has…
f: Speaker Unnati Ved is the co-founder of The Lit People, a thriving book club in Hyderabad. She is an ELT professional and the founder of Eager Readers, an enrichment academy for learners of 5 to 16 years, which has reading and activity clubs, writing clubs, speech and drama clubs, current affairs clubs, teacher training, and school tie-ups.
